picks.headline: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Texas Tech Athletics Texas Tech hosts Arizona in this big time Big 12 showdown. The Texas Tech Red Raiders need to focus on boosting their offense for this one. Quarterback Will Hammond has 1,561 passing yards, but he has thrown only six touchdowns and has six interceptions on the season. Explosive running back J'Koby Williams has 619 rushing yards and 5 TDs, but if you take away the Arizona State and Oregon State games, he has been inconsistent for the Red Raiders this season. Kenny Johnson , a receiver, is the main downfield target but only has one touchdown reception this season and, besides the Houston and Arizona State games, has not had a significant impact on the Texas Tech passing attack. All three as well as some other key offensive players need to step up and have big games against Arizona to win this game. The defense has to get back to focusing and dominating like they have for a lot of the season. The Red Raiders have one of the most ball-hawking secondary units in the country, sitting near the top of NCAA FBS with 13 interceptions. Defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. anchors the front seven and has 6 sacks this season. However, the Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season, a 37-24 loss to Cincinnati where they gave up 427 yards and gave up four passing touchdowns. They will be seeking to bounce back at home to stay undefeated at home this season. Arizona, on the other hand, has a five-game winning streak and defeated Cincinnati by a final score of 34-7. Their only loss of the season was to BYU on the road. Veteran quarterback Noah Fifita leads the Arizona Wildcats, who again have a high-efficiency passing offense, with Fifiti already having 2,064 passing yards and 18 TDs through seven games. Kedrick Reescano leads the ground game with just over 300 rushing yards and five touchdowns, while wideout Isaiah Mizell is an explosive playmaker with 493 yards and 5 TDs this season, most of which have come in the Wildcats' last two games against Iowa State and West Virginia. Linebacker Taye Brown has a team-leading 27 tackles and leads the Wildcats defense. Edge rusher Chase Kennedy leads the team in pressure rate with 4 sacks, and the Texas Tech offensive line has a tough task trying to stop him from getting to the quarterback. Arizona has a scoring defense that gives up only 16.7 points per game, but they did give up 31 points against West Virginia. Arizona recently crushed Iowa State 39-3 and has put up a total of just over 200 points in their last five games. The Wildcats are also 2-1 on the road this season heading into Lubbock for this top 25 game. The key matchup for this game will be Noah Fifita vs. the Texas Tech secondary. Fifita’s efficient throwing (almost 74% completion rate) will face immediate tests from a Red Raider defense that excels at creating takeaways via interceptions. Another major matchup in this game pits the Red Raiders offensive line against Arizona’s front seven on defense. Texas Tech’s running offense behind J’Koby Williams and Quinten Joyner will face a challenge against an Arizona front seven that is holding opponents under 110 rushing yards per game. This game also has Big 12 Championship ramifications since both teams are deadlocked at 3-1 in conference play behind undefeated Utah, and the winner is squarely in the race for a Big 12 Championship Game berth. An early game prediction for this game that may change slightly as the injury reports for both teams come out later this week, but the Red Raiders bounce back and win a very close game by a final score of Texas Tech 28, Arizona 27. Pete Fiutak Tue, October 27, 2026 at 11:28 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas Tech was cruising right along, looking like the star of the Big 12 again after a 53-25 blowout over Arizona State, and then it walked into a wall at Cincinnati, losing with a 37-24 thud. Arizona has been fantastic ever since its 28-17 loss at BYU early in the season, including a 34-7 win over Cincinnati. But it still has a few nasty games to go in November. Both teams are 6-1. The winner will be set up nicely for a College Football Playoff spot if it doesn't win the Big 12 title. The loser will still be alive for the CFP if it wins out, but getting to the Big 12 Championship in a loaded conference season will be tough. Arizona vs Texas Tech: Quick Hits Texas Tech still has to go to Oklahoma State, but it doesn't have to face BYU or Utah, and the other three games against West Virginia, at Baylor, and TCU aren't bad. Arizona gets three of its final four games at home, getting TCU and Utah next before going to Kansas State and finishing up against Arizona State. Texas Tech won the most recent matchup 28-22 in 2024 and is 5-2-1 in the series going back to 1975. How To Watch Arizona vs Texas Tech Arizona at Texas Tech Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, TX – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Arizona Will Win For the second time all year, Texas Tech played someone who could run well, and Cincinnati went off in the 13-point win. Houston can run. It ran 37 times for 175 yards against the Red Raiders, and lost when it couldn't hit a late two-point conversion. Cincinnati wasn't exactly more physical, but it found space on the way to a 255-yard day with big run after big run. Arizona's running game isn't a killer, but it's more than effective enough, working hand-in-hand with super-accurate quarterback Noah Fifita and an offense that's great at keeping the chains moving. Why Texas Tech Will Win Arizona doesn't take the ball away enough, and that matters in a huge way here. The Wildcats forced two takeaways in the win over Washington State, and two more in the win over West Virginia. That's about it, coming up with six on the year. Texas Tech has a huge problem with turnovers, with three against Cincinnati, two against Houston, and ten in the last five games. Don't turn it over, or at least stay even in the mistake battle, and the Red Raiders should be fine. Texas Tech has a great balance to its attack, and it needs to mix it up. BYU and West Virginia – in very different ways – both showed it's possible to move the ball efficiently against the Wildcat defense. Arizona vs Texas Tech Prediction, Betting Lines Is Arizona ready to show that it's really and truly a player, or will Texas Tech wipe away the Cincinnati loss like it was just a blip? It'll be a little of both, as Arizona controls the clock and tempo for the first half, but Texas Tech gets the pass rush working early in the second half. It'll be rough for the Red Raiders without pressuring Fifita, and they won't do enough of it over the final ten minutes. picks.blurb: Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 28, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football College football has one of the longest offseasons of any sport, which lends itself to certain players and teams generating a lot of hype and attention. Texas Tech falls squarely in that category, as its seemingly unlimited resources thanks to billionaire booster Cody Campbell made it a go-to place for top transfers out of the portal. But that also led to the ill-fated acquisition of quarterback Brendan Sorsby , who after leaving Cincinnati for Tech was revealed to have bet on college sports. Sorsby was banned by the NCAA, later reinstated, but the backlash led to him leaving the program before ever playing a game. Despite that, Tech was unbeaten before losing last week, dropping to No. 13 in the AP poll and into a tie for second place in the Big 12 with, among other teams, Arizona. That in effect makes Saturday’s matchup an unofficial elimination game for the conference title race. To better understand the Red Raiders, we reached out to Seth Jungman of Staking the Plains for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his eloquent answers to our inarticulate questions: AZ Desert Swarm: Outside of the irony of the first loss coming to Cincinnati, what were the biggest contributors to Texas Tech falling from the ranks of the unbeatens? Seth Jungman: “It’s the thing that I think Texas Tech fans have known, but maybe the national media wasn’t paying attention. I think most fans have known that the offense simply wasn’t very good and the defense isn’t as good as it was last year. Will Hammond is fine, but there’s a reason why the staff went out to get Brendan Sorsby before the season. They knew he probably wasn’t ready, but things happened and here we are. Also, I think it’s incredibly evident that the players who were part of this defense last year were truly special, particularly Jacob Rodriguez, David Bailey, and Romello Height. Getting to the quarterback to wreck offenses was the cheat code last year and this year, that’s simply not happening.” It’s fair to say that Will Hammond was not the first choice to lead this offense. How do you think he has performed to this point? What are his best attributes and where does he lack most? “I thought last week against Arizona State he took a step forward, but against Cincinnati he took two steps back. His best attributes is that he is a natural leader and he wants the ball in his hands and he wants to be the guy. My biggest problem with him is that I think he makes bad game management decisions. Knowing that the team needs points, he’ll heave the ball towards the end zone with a low chance of completion rather than take the play that keeps the drive alive. His lack of understanding of knowing when to take chances and when to churn yards is what bothers me the most.” What is the likelihood that Cameron Dickey will be back for this game? How would that impact the run game and the way J’Koby Williams, who has run for 680 yards and five touchdowns, get used? “I think chances are very good that he returns. It’s been about four weeks from the dreaded high-ankle sprain and that’s about the time. I don’t think it was a bad sprain so this game would seem about right and he was out doing some drills this past week. What Dickey offers is a guy that’s going to bruise and batter the opposing defense while Williams will break a 40-yard run in what looks like a lost play. Quinten Joyner has tried to fill that roll for Dickey, but it’s not the same. Joyner is coming off of ACL surgery and he doesn’t have the same burst he had at USC. I think the staff will likely get back to that Dickey-Williams rotation as soon as possible.” Texas Tech is second in FBS in passes intercepted (13) but has also given up 16 TD passes and is ranked third-worst in the Big 12 in pass defense. How do you expect the defense to try and stop Noah Fifita? “As mentioned above, the Texas Tech defense last year was getting to the quarterback so quickly that teams simply could not function offensively. This year . . . not so much. Fifita has rounded out to be such a good quarterback, I truly expect him to have a very good day. There’s almost no difference between his home and road stats, three picks on the road and just one at home, and he’s throwing for nearly 300 yards every time he steps on the field. That’s the kind of consistency that you expect from a senior and with Fifita’s ability to run to keep the defense honest, I expect him to do what he’s done all year long.” Who are the top defensive players that Arizona has to be most concerned with? “Defensive tackle AJ Holmes is an absolute unit and there aren’t a ton of defensive tackles that truly rush the passer, but he’s one of them. The linebacking corps is incredibly solid with Ben Roberts, John Curry and Austin Romaine. I’ll also add in Brice Pollock at cornerback. The pass defense is struggling a bit, but he’s a solid cornerback that can make plays.” Considering all the money that was spent on this team, and all the national attention it has brought on itself—thanks, Cody Campbell!—does it feel like the season is on the line in this game? How do you expect Tech to respond to that last performance? “As you have already recognized, this team is a quarterback short of maybe what it could have been. I try not to involve myself in the offseason drama. The whole thing was a mess and handled poorly. I think we’ve all moved on, but I know it still lingers and I think that Sorsby would have made a significant difference in the offense. For what Joey McGuire preaches, yes, the season is on the brink because the goal is to win the Big 12 and make the playoffs. I don’t know that a Big 12 team with two losses makes the playoff and I also don’t think that a 2-loss Big 12 team makes the championship. “I do expect Texas Tech to play much better than what they did against Cincinnati and I think it will be a much more competitive game. I also realize that Arizona’s defense is no joke and the Texas Tech offense has really only played well against defenses that aren’t very good. The offense and defense for the Red Raiders have a lot to prove against Arizona.” Prediction time. Does Arizona end the Red Raiders’ 12-game home win streak and continue its push toward the Big 12 title game or does Texas Tech get back on track? Give us a score pick. “My gut tells me that this will be an incredibly close game and Vegas thinks so as well. With a touchdown advantage, the line now sits at Texas Tech -3.5. I tend to agree, that despite the flaws that were on display against Cincinnati, I think Texas Tech does win the game, but I’d take Arizona and those points. Something like 37-34 is what I see the final score being.” Next 3 weeks could decide Big 12 football title game participants Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. picks.blurb: Arizona vs. Texas Tech Prediction, Pick and Odds for Week 9 Teams Arizona Wildcats Arizona State Sun Devils Cincinnati Bearcats Colorado Buffaloes Houston Cougars Iowa State Cyclones Kansas Jayhawks Kansas State Wildcats Oklahoma State Cowboys TCU Horned Frogs Texas Tech Red Raiders West Virginia Mountaineers Former Foes Missouri Tigers Nebraska Cornhuskers Oklahoma Sooners Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Recruiting Football Transfer Portal Video Watch on YouTube Listen on Apple Listen on Spotify Forum Members Login Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today The Arizona Wildcats and Texas Tech Red Raiders meet on Saturday in Lubbock in a Top 25 showdown that could have major implications on the Big 12 Championship race. Both teams enter Week 9 at 6-1 overall and 3-1 in Big 12 play, but they're coming off completely different Saturdays. Arizona made another statement by crushing Iowa State 39-3, while Texas Tech suffered its first loss of the season in a 37-24 road defeat at Cincinnati. Now, Texas Tech returns home to a place where it has won 12 straight games, while Arizona gets another opportunity to prove it belongs among the top contenders in the Big 12. The matchup also features an intriguing battle between Noah Fifita and an aggressive Texas Tech defense that leads the country with five pick-sixes this season. Here is everything you need to know about Arizona vs. Texas Tech in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Saturday's Big 12 showdown. Texas Tech vs. Arizona Odds Spread: Texas Tech -3.5 Over/Under: 54.5 Moneyline: Arizona +134/Texas Tech -160 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: Arizona's Passing Game vs. Texas Tech's Defense? The Red Raiders' defense has been underwhelming, at best. Texas Tech ranks 14th in the Big 12 Conference in passing yards allowed per game, ranking only ahead of Cincinnati and West Virginia. Now, this secondary does have 13 takeaways, which is tops in the Big 12. But that also tells me that they may be too aggressive , at times. And now they have to slow down Noah Fifita, who doesn't make many mistakes. He's thrown 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions this season and has the deepest wide receiver corps in the entire Big 12. Whoever wins this match up will win the game. Houston vs. Utah Prediction and Pick Prediction: Arizona 31, Texas Tech 24 Texas Tech was exposed last week at Cincinnati. Yes, they have talent, but they haven't been able to put it all together this season. And after Saturday, there's no evidence that it's magically going to happen against one of the most underrated teams in the country, Arizona, who is playing some of the best football in America right now. Since losing to BYU on the road (a game they led in the second half), Arizona has won five-straight games by an average of nearly 24 points. I haven't even talked about the other side of the ball, where Arizona is Top 5 in passing defense in yards allowed per game, and ranked 3rd in the Big 12 in yards allowed per carry (3.1). The front seven has been outstanding, as that impressive run defense has done it against the Top 2 rushing offenses in the league (West Virginia, Cincinnati). They've racked up 24 sacks in seven games, good for second in the Big 12, and now take on a Texas Tech offensive line that has been spotty, at best, throughout the season. Also, in a game that could come down to the final drive or two, Arizona's red zone defense ranks tops in the Big 12, while Texas Tech comes in at No. 14. And as the game wears on, the Tech defense could get worn down. Tech is second-to-last in the Big 12 in Time of Possession, while Arizona is in the Top 5, this despite having a pass-heavy offense. The icing on the cake on my pick? Special teams. Arizona is the best punt returning team in the Big 12. Texas Tech ranks 13th. These little things in a tough Top 25 match up can be the difference. And they will be come Saturday in Lubbock. And if you want to know where the sharp money is: 62% of the tickets are on Texas Tech, but over 80% of the money is on Arizona. The line opened up at Arizona +4.5 and is down to +3.5. If you can still get more than a field goal, jump on it. Arizona wins. Arizona covers. Sure, the Red Raiders are tough at home. Nobody's arguing that. But Arizona just beat Iowa State 39-3, and Texas Tech went to Cincinnati and lost 37-24. That's a pretty big difference in how these two teams spent their Saturday. And here's the part I keep coming back to. Arizona beat that same Cincinnati team 34-7 earlier this month. Doesn't mean the Wildcats automatically win in Lubbock, but it sure makes me question anyone treating Texas Tech like the obvious choice. Be prepared for all the college action with our free college football picks . Arizona visits Texas Tech at Galaxy Stadium in Lubbock on Saturday, October 31, 2026. Kickoff is scheduled for noon ET, with television coverage on ABC or ESPN. BetMGM has Texas Tech favored by 3.5 points, with the total sitting at 54.5. Both teams are fighting for position in the Big 12, and I think we're getting a much closer game than some Texas Tech fans might expect. Arizona Wildcats Have More Than Enough Offense to Win This Game Arizona is 6-1 overall and 2-1 on the road. The Wildcats have won five straight, and that 39-3 beating they handed Iowa State was probably their best performance yet. They finished with 477 yards while allowing only 221. Iowa State never really got anything going after the opening quarter. What impressed me was how Arizona handled the game once it got ahead. The Wildcats didn't start giving away possessions or letting Iowa State back into it. They kept playing football. That's what you want from a team heading into a difficult road game. The offense has scored at least 34 points in five straight games. Arizona put up 52 at West Virginia and 34 against Cincinnati before handling Iowa State. The passing game has been the difference. The Wildcats threw for 336 yards Saturday, and they've shown they can score without having to pound the ball between the tackles all afternoon. That's important against Texas Tech because the Red Raiders can be awfully difficult to run against. Arizona's defense deserves some credit, too. Holding Cincinnati to seven points looks a whole lot better after watching the Bearcats score 37 against Tech. I wouldn't expect Arizona to shut the Red Raiders down completely, but the Wildcats have shown they can get stops against good competition. Sign Up Get $30 Premium Picks Credit + Exclusive Offers Noah Fifita is the guy I'd trust to keep Arizona in this game. He's thrown for 2,064 yards with 18 touchdowns and only four interceptions, and he just completed 27 of 34 passes against Iowa State. That's pretty efficient football. Isaiah Mizell has 493 receiving yards and five touchdowns, including that 71-yard score Saturday. Kendrick Reescano has five rushing touchdowns, giving Arizona another way to finish drives. The Wildcats do have injuries at receiver, with Giovanni Richardson and Chris Hunter dealing with problems, while Tre Spivey remains out. That's something to watch because Texas Tech can get after the quarterback. But if Fifita has time to throw, I like his chances of moving the ball. Texas Tech Red Raiders Need a Better Game From Their Quarterback Texas Tech is 6-1 overall and 4-0 at home. That's a good football team, and I wouldn't pretend otherwise. The Red Raiders beat Arizona State 53-25 two weeks ago and looked like they could score whenever they felt like it. Then Cincinnati happened. Tech trailed 24-6 at halftime and never recovered, losing 37-24. I expect a better effort back in Lubbock. The Red Raiders have played well there all season, and a loss like that usually gets everybody's attention at practice. But I'm not ready to forget how badly things went in Cincinnati just because they're coming home. Texas Tech's defense can cause real problems when the pass rush gets going. The Red Raiders sacked Arizona State six times, and that's exactly the kind of afternoon that could make things difficult for Fifita. If Tech gets pressure without sending extra defenders, Arizona could have trouble sustaining drives. But the Red Raiders aren't impossible to move the ball against. Cincinnati showed that last weekend, and Arizona has a much better passing attack than people sometimes give it credit for. Tech also needs to run the ball well enough to keep Arizona from focusing entirely on its quarterback. If this turns into Hammond throwing on every down, I like the Wildcats' chances of forcing a mistake. Will Hammond has thrown for 1,561 yards, but his six touchdowns and six interceptions aren't exactly numbers that make me want to lay points against a good defense. He threw an interception and lost a fumble against Cincinnati. Those mistakes hurt when you're trying to come from behind. J'Koby Williams has been a bright spot with 619 rushing yards and five touchdowns, and Kenny Johnson has 499 receiving yards. There's plenty of talent here. Cameron Dickey and Donte Lee Jr. remain sidelined, though, and Jalen Jones has also been dealing with an injury. Texas Tech can win this game with the players it has available. I just think it'll have to earn every bit of it. Arizona vs Texas Tech Picks and Predictions Arizona Wildcats +3.5 I'm taking Arizona plus the 3.5 points, and I wouldn't be surprised if the Wildcats win outright. The biggest reason is Fifita. He's playing well, he's protecting the football, and Arizona has scored 34 or more in five straight games. Texas Tech has a dangerous pass rush, and I'll admit that worries me. Six sacks against Arizona State is no joke. But Tech also just gave up 37 points to Cincinnati, a team Arizona held to seven. I'm not saying those results tell us exactly what happens Saturday. They don't. But they tell me Arizona belongs on the same field with the Red Raiders. Texas Tech might get a couple of big plays at home, and Williams could have a good afternoon running the ball. I still trust Fifita more than Hammond if this comes down to a couple of late possessions. Give me the Wildcats and the points. I like Over 54.5 here, although the side is my stronger play. Arizona has been putting points on the board every week, and Texas Tech has enough offensive talent to answer. The Red Raiders scored 53 against Arizona State and have been particularly dangerous at home. Arizona's defense has been good, but I don't expect it to hold Tech to seven the way it did Cincinnati. On the other side, Fifita should find opportunities against a defense that gave up 37 last weekend. The concern is Texas Tech getting enough pressure to wreck Arizona's passing game. If Fifita spends the afternoon running for his life, the over could be in trouble. But I think both teams reach the upper 20s, and that should be enough. Something around Arizona 30-28 wouldn't surprise me. Final Picks: Arizona Wildcats +3.5 and Over 54.5 Betting on College Football? away.headline: K-State QB Avery Johnson listed as doubtful for Arizona State in Friday update
away.blurb: Kansas State quarterback Avery Johnson will enter game day listed as doubtful for the Wildcats' matchup with Arizona State in Tempe, after he maintained the injury designation in Friday night's report. Johnson has been listed as questionable since appearing on the team's initial Wednesday report. The Wildcats play the Sun Devils on Saturday, Oct. 24, at 2:45 p.m. CT in Tempe, Arizona. This article originally appeared on Topeka Capital-Journal: K-State QB Avery Johnson listed as doubtful for Arizona State in Friday update Johnson missed one play early in the first quarter of the Wildcats' win over Kansas last week after stumbling to the turf at the end of a long run. He returned the following drive and played the remainder of the game without any signs of injury. Kansas State football coach Collin Klein did not address, and was not asked about, any injury concerns regarding his quarterback during his weekly radio show on Wednesday ahead of the report being released. Kansas State could be forced to start backup Jacob Knuth, who handed the ball off to Rodney Fields for a four-yard touchdown on the one play Johnson missed. Knuth is a fifth-year player who entered this season having appeared in four games across three seasons in Manhattan. This year, he's played snaps against Nicholls, Washington State and Kansas, completing one pass for seven yards, along with three rushes for 25 yards and a score. Kansas State has dealt with backup quarterback injuries throughout this season. Barnett has been on crutches since the Wildcats' Week 1 win over Nicholls. Sophomore Dillon Duff has appeared on the injury report each week since the Wildcats' Sept. 26 loss at Cincinnati and didn't dress for the first three games. The Wildcats will release a final availability report on Saturday at 1:15 p.m. CT. Wyatt D. Wheeler covers Kansas State athletics for the USA TODAY Network and Topeka Capital-Journal. A three-year starter, Johnson is in the middle of perhaps his best collegiate season. He has completed 118 of 187 passes for 1,301 yards with 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. Last week he had a huge day in the victory against the Kansas Jayhawks. He completed 14 of 24 passes for 209 yards and a touchdown. He also had 132 yards rushing on 12 carries in the 35-24 victory against the Jayhawks. The Wildcats could use Johnson in a game they hope can continue to build momentum this season. After a two-game losing streak (against the Cincinnati Bearcats and Houston Cougars) to start the Big 12 schedule, they bounced back with a big victory against Kansas. A win against the Sun Devils would give the Wildcats a two-game winning streak in the conference. It would also keep them in the race for the Big 12 title game and a berth in the College Football Playoff. All of the signs are pointing toward Johnson playing this weekend in Tempe. The hope is Johnson is ready to go to help the Wildcats' chance of moving three games ahead of .500.

He and Tabb are the one-two punch that drives the Cincy offense. If Payne is not at full strength, they may be limited in their ability to ground and pound against a good Texas Tech run defense. That's because Payne is their workhorse. Texas Tech football could catch a big break with a key Cincinnati injury Skip to main content About Just yesterday, we discussed the strength of the Cincinnati Bearcats' ground game as we look ahead to this weekend's matchup for the Texas Tech football team. When Saturday arrives, the Bearcats may be missing a key component to their attack, though, as running back Gi'Bran Payne is listed on the first injury report of the week. He entered that game leading the Bearcats in rushing with 392 yards to go along with two touchdowns. But against the Mountaineers, he carried the ball just seven times for 26 yards. Still, the Bearcats were able to rack up 233 yards on the ground against a putrid West Virginia defense. Junior Cole Tabb picked up the slack, amassing 188 yards and two touchdowns on just 15 rushes. Senior QB JC French IV also chipped in with 53 yards and a rushing touchdown on 13 carries. Overall, the Bearcats run for an average of 231.2 yards per game. That's the 11th-most in the entire country. Certainly, their plan this weekend is to try to keep the ball away from the Red Raider offense and protect their defense that ranks just 128th in the country in yards allowed per game. But to do that, they will likely need a healthy Payne to pair with Tabb. Both Payne and Tabb have run for over 400 yards this season. In all, Cincy averages 39 rushing attempts per game while throwing the ball only 33.8 times per game. Though Tabb now has more yards on the season (448 compared to Payne's 418), Payne has carried the ball 20 more times this season. Tabb is only 5-foot-8 and 200 pounds, meaning he is more of a big-play weapon similar to Texas Tech's J'Koby Williams. Meanwhile, Payne is a bit bigger at 5-foot-10 and around 210 pounds. He functions as the between-the-tackles runner who picks up tough yards when needed, something that is crucial in a run-first, ball-control offense. Thus, his potential absence could alter the way Cincinnati tries to move the football on Saturday, So keep an eye on the Cincinnati injury report. home.blurb: Texas Tech RB Expected to Return from Injury vs. Arizona - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF TRADE DEADLINE: Colts WR Josh Downs reportedly wants out amid fire sale Texas Tech RB Expected to Return from Injury vs. Arizona After going through the bye week and missing Tech's next two games - a blowout win over Arizona State and an underwhelming loss at Cincinnati - Dickey is on track to return to Joey McGuire's lineup for the ranked clash with fellow one-loss Big 12 foe Arizona on Saturday. "He's so consistent, so reliable," Tech offensive coordinator Mack Leftwich said of Dickey. "He's so versatile because you can do a bunch of stuff with him out of the backfield and as a blocker. He's great at blitz pickup, which will be huge this week. Getting him back will be a big boost for us for sure and just gives us good depth in that room." "All those kinds of things are on the table and trying to figure out what those things you know when you talk about simplifying the passing game," Leftwich added. "Especially what type of reads he does best and just really honing in on what we can do well." Perhaps the easiest offensive fix is getting Cam Dickey available again out of the backfield. TRENDING Rays rally, avoid sweep (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Nathan Karseno Tue, October 27, 2026 at 11:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads LUBBOCK -- Texas Tech's bruising running back Cam Dickey injured his left ankle in the Red Raiders' road win over Colorado on Oct. 3. "He should be good to go," McGuire said about Dickey this week. The all-conference ball carrier from a year ago entered this season amidst a three-man committee next to J'Koby Williams and Quinten Joyner. While the former USC transfer Joyner has been up and down in his first season on the field following last year's preseason injury, Dickey has been the "thunder" to Williams' "lightning", making for an interesting rushing attack for Texas Tech. That ground game has also featured fifth-year quarterback transfer Thomas Castellanos, though McGuire admitted to his mistake in not putting Castellanos in his typical short-yardage, low red zone spots in the loss to the Bearcats this weekend. No. 13-ranked Texas Tech's offense could get a major boost with Dickey back in the lineup against No. 22 Arizona on Halloween afternoon (11 a.m. CT kickoff on ESPN). "We should get him with a full [practice on] Wednesday, unless he has any setbacks," McGuire said. "I know he looked good last week, and so it's going to be good to have him back. Just another guy that's been in some big games that's got a lot of experience and a lot of juice." This season, the junior Dickey has rushed for 249 yards and four touchdowns. It's not going to dominate against this Badger defense, but … Wisconsin isn't completing passes. This will be about field position, mistakes, and one big play in a tough dogfight. home.headline: Starting safety Zach Lutmer gave a crucial status update before Iowa battles for Floyd
home.blurb: Starting safety Zach Lutmer has established himself as one of the defense's leaders and is still adjusting to being a full-time safety. Lutmer has played well, but he has been hampered by a few injuries, including another injury against Washington. Lutmer was limited to three tackles after suffering an injury, but he gave a great update before Iowa heads to Minneapolis . Lutmer revealed that he feels "quite a bit better" after the bye week, and he feels like himself again. If Lutmer is close to 100 percent, that is big news for the defense, which is already down one starting safety. Tyler Brown is still out for an undetermined amount of time and was listed as "Out" on Iowa's initial injury report . Xavier Styles played well opposite Lutmer in week six, and will likely get the start against Minnesota, but losing two starting safeties would have been devastating to an already thin group. If it wasn't for a fluke game in 2023, when Iowa was forced to use quarterback Deacon Hill and Cooper DeJean's game-winning punt-return touchdown was called back, Iowa would have been 10-0. 9-1 is solid, and to keep the streak alive, the defense must step up and hold the Golden Gophers' offense down. Iowa obliterated Lindsey last season, forcing him to throw two interceptions, including a pick-six. The game plan has to be the same, especially against an inconsistent rushing attack. Iowa has multiple things going for it, and Lutmer is a big part of that. The Golden Gophers know the Hawkeyes very well, and they will try to keep the defense off balance. Slowing down the run and forcing Lindsey to pass more often is a solid strategy, and it will be interesting to see if Iowa continues its dominating run against Minnesota.

Here is this week's Behind Enemy Lines featuring Sam Hutchens of The Clarion-Ledger. What was your biggest takeaway from Ole Miss' recent loss to Texas? SH: "Ole Miss isn't good enough to dig itself out of huge holes. The Rebels were close to doing it in Austin, but Pete Golding was correct when he said they need to be more consistent." Kewan Lacy will not play on Saturday. What does the Ole Miss run game look like without him? SH: "There's a chance it's still pretty good. Makhi Frazier and JT Lindsey have been serviceable backups all year. Look for young Shekai Mills-Knight, who absolutely could be a future RB1 in the SEC, to get more carries too" A handful of former Tigers are with Ole Miss now, including Horatio Fields and Jay Crawford. How much impact have they made since joining the team? Do you expect either of them to dictate the outcome of Saturday's game? SH: "Both players have been solid transfer portal adds. Fields has been a little bit of an unexpected bright spot. He has the second-most catches on the team among receivers, behind Deuce Alexander. Going into the year, he wasn't the player many projected as the WR2." Which Tigers have your attention ahead of the game? SH: "Byrum Brown is the player I'm most excited to see. The Ole Miss rushing defense has been vulnerable at times this season, and the Rebels haven't generated pressure consistently. Maybe a recipe for Brown to shine." Ole Miss wins on Saturday if.... SH: "It turns the ball over one time or less. The Rebels are fantastic in home games over the past few seasons. They don't need a perfect game to win, but they must avoid self-inflicted errors." By Parker Gillam Published: Oct 27, 2026 · 8:56 PM EDT The grind of the 9-game SEC schedule has taken its toll on every team in the league, and nobody knows that better than Auburn and Ole Miss . Both the Tigers and Rebels have enjoyed incredible highs and head-scratching lows this season, with the former having upset Georgia then blown out by LSU the next week while the latter has gone from taking down those same Bayou Bengals to getting trampled by Florida, then returning the favor to Missouri before falling in Austin last weekend. All of that is to say that when Auburn and Ole Miss square off Saturday, each will be desperate for a victory. ESPN's Bill Connelly's SP+ cares not about desperation, instead trusting a series of metrics and simulations to predict games each week. And regarding the clash in Oxford, SP+ believes that the Rebels should be able to bounce back with a 32-21 win over the visiting Tigers, keeping their College Football Playoff hopes intact for just a bit longer ahead of some tough matchups down the stretch. away.headline: LSU football injury report puts Auburn's tackles under the gun
away.blurb: LSU will see EDGE Princewill Umanmielen's return to the field this coming Saturday after his name was not on the injury report for the Auburn game. Jacob Strand, who was formerly playing in the interior earlier this season, has gotten significant snaps at left tackle of late. He and Jo Simmons have a massive test this coming week against Umanmielen, who was previously questionable after missing most of the game against Mississippi State with an upper-body injury. We'll see if the Auburn offensive line is ready to protect quarterback Byrum Brown against it. Stanton Ramil graded out as an 80 on the right edge against Georgia in the epic Deep South's Oldest Rivalry upset . The interior held up remarkably well, with Wilson Zierer and Kenneth McManus taking starter snaps. Brown and Jeremiah Cobb showed out against the Dawgs with their best outings of the season. Auburn's run game could have a symbiotic effect with the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd and keep the pressure on LSU's defense. LSU football injury report puts Auburn's tackles under the gun Skip to main content About Alex Golesh, Joel Gordon, and Tyler Hudanick must now prepare for a physical freak with a 4.7-second 40-yard dash and an elite bend on Blake Baker's defense. The Ole Miss transfer Umanmielen immediately puts one of Golesh's recent big decisions to the test. Alex Golesh understands the challenge LSU is on the edge As Golesh said about LSU, "Those edges are real, like real real." Not only is Umanmielen a handful, but Tennessee transfer Jordan Ross is also elite. Ross had six tackles and a sack against State this past Saturday. Ross has three sacks this year, which ranks third behind defensive tackle Deuce Geralds's five and Umanmielen's eight. The group is even playing without Gabriel Reliford, who tore his ACL in the spring. The roster Lane Kiffin recruited has an embarrassment of riches in Baton Rouge. Auburn's run game has breakout chance against LSU Umanmielen isn't as renowned against the run. With that said, LSU's defense is better overall against the run than the pass. If you're looking for ways to nab an upset on Saturday and prove the Plains is haunted for favored opponents , controlling the clock is one of the most obvious. Brown is the ultimate wild card for Auburn. If he can keep LSU's defense guessing, opening up running lanes in the middle for Auburn when LSU's linebackers drop into coverage, perhaps Cobb, Omar Mabson, and the rest of the running backs could be difference-makers in a pivotal SEC clash.

home.blurb: Texas star edge Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful for Saturday’s matchup after sustaining a high ankle sprain in the loss to Florida, while running back Hollywood Smothers is listed as questionable. Smothers reportedly missed practice on Monday due to a shoulder injury. Other names listed for the Longhorns are wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman (both questionable), as well as freshman edge Richard Wesley (out). Simmons going down during the Florida game is a huge blow for the Texas defense, as he has been playing at an extremely high level. Texas defensive coordinator Will Muschamp is going to need all hands on deck on Saturday to defend Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who has been one of the most dynamic playmakers in the country at the quarterback position, especially with the surprise news that Wesley is out. On top of that, Ole Miss will likely have star running back Kewan Lacy back on the field, as he is listed as probable on tonight’s injury report. The initial SEC injury report was released for the Saturday matchup between the No. 19 Texas Longhorns and against the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels on Wednesday and while the Rebels have many more players on their side of the injury report, there are certainly some notable names for the Longhorns as well. Every game moving forward is a must-win for the Longhorns after dropping the last two matchups. They will need to get healthy moving forward as they try to navigate a difficult stretch in the schedule with eight straight games to close the season.

(AP) — Mississippi running back Kewan Lacy will miss this week's game against Auburn after dislocating his shoulder during the third quarter of Ole Miss' loss to Texas , Rebels coach Pete Golding said Monday. "It wasn't exactly what it was before, it was different," Golding said. "Obviously, he's not going to play this week." Recurring injuries to the left shoulder have troubled the preseason All-America selection , who rushed for 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns during the 2025 season. A separate shoulder injury during a victory over LSU followed a lower leg injury in the season-opening win over Louisville . Lacy was sidelined against Florida before an open date and a seven-carry performance at Vanderbilt . Lacy had a season-high 122 yards in a victory over Missouri before the injury against the Longhorns. "We're going to evaluate that moving forward, kind of what it looks like," Golding said of Lacy's prospects for returning to the field later this season. "But there's no chance that we're going to try that at all this week." Lacy has rushed for 352 yards and five touchdowns this season. In his absence, Ole Miss is expected to deploy a four-player rotation headed by Michigan State transfer junior Makhi Frazier. Senior Joshua Dye and sophomores JT Lindsey and Shekai Mills-Knight have played in reserve roles, but Frazier has gotten extensive playing time, rushing for 301 yards. "We're going to need all those guys moving forward," Golding said. "We need to do a good job in that room creating roles for them, allow them to execute throughout the week so we can play better on Saturday." Ole Miss RB out with shoulder injury suffered in Texas game Skip to main content About Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding ruled out Rebels running back Kewan Lacy on Monday for a Week 9 matchup with Auburn in Oxford, Mississippi, this Halloween. Lacy suffered the injury during a 34-27 loss to Texas in Austin this past Saturday evening. Before the injury, Lacy was averaging 2.2 yards per carry and produced just 42 yards of offense against the Longhorns. Lacy missed the Florida game in Week 4, a matchup Ole Miss lost 52-28 in Gainesville , with a different injury to the same shoulder. After the Texas game, Golding sounded concerned about Lacy making it to the field against the Tigers because it was a previously problematic shoulder. "I've not got an update on that... Obviously, I was on the field with him. He was in a lot of pain. Same shoulder, so hopefully we’ll get updates soon," Golding said postgame about Lacy's injury. Golding didn't sound overly optimistic then, and now we see why. Who is Ole Miss's starting running back against Auburn? Without Lacy, Michigan State transfer Makhi Frazier will step into the workhorse role for the Rebels against Auburn. Frazier had 47 rushing yards on six carries and 16 receiving yards on five catches against the Longhorns. For the year, Frazier is averaging 5.9 yards per carry, with 301 yards on the ground total. Golding explained in the spring why having an experienced running back transfer like Frazier would come in handy for the offense. "We wanted some (running backs) with some experience, which we brought in," Golding said. "You feel like regardless whether you are going the one, two, three or four up there, it's like 'Man, this kid's got a chance.' You don't see that drop-off that I've felt like we have before." Golding's emergency preparedness paid off against a Tigers defense that is particularly susceptible to the run, as Tennessee's DeSean Bishop and Florida's Jadan Baugh can attest to. The pair had 382 rushing yards in the two AU losses. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and running back Dilin Jones both got their licks in this past Saturday during a 38-17 blowout win for the Bayou Bengals at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Leavitt had 54 rushing yards on eight carries with a touchdown, while Jones had 92 yards on the ground and a touchdown run. Golding isn't taking Auburn lightly , and with Lacy down, he has extra incentive to treat Saturday as a make-or-break game.

Both teams enter the game ranked for the first time since 2020, which is also the last time the Gators won it. UF (5-2, 3-2 in SEC) comes in hot after its second win over a top-10 team this season, a 27-24 victory at Texas . Backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. impressed with two touchdown passes and the game-sealing run, raising questions over whether he or Aaron Philo will get the start this week. Georgia (6-1, 4-1) fell from the ranks of the unbeaten two weeks ago when Byrum Brown spurred a late drive that led to Auburn's unbelievable 27-24 in Athens. The obvious mismatch in this game comes through the air. UGA has a top-30 passing offense that has eight players with at least 100 yards receiving. UF fields a bottom-20 pass defense that allowed two straight embarrassing losses before the big Texas win. Florida has been able to counteract its deficiencies by getting to the quarterback, tying Georgia for third in the SEC with 22 sacks. UGA has protected Stockton well, though, allowing just eight sacks all year. The Gators' other big strength — Jadan Baugh and their 30th-ranked rushing attack — can also be undone by the Dawgs with their No. 10 run defense. The Gators have been up and down this season. They looked dominant in a 52-28 win over Ole Miss before losing back-to-back games to Missouri and South Carolina. "Look, Georgia goes for it less than any team in the FBS on fourth down, and they run fewer plays per game than most teams in the country. That's a formula for winning comfortably without covering a massive number because punts and field goals leave the door ajar, and if Georgia gets ahead early, then Smart will happily sit on it and try to pound away. "So here's what I'm thinking: these are the two biggest matchups in the game and they both belong to Georgia's offense. The short passing game against a defense that has struggled to stop it, and third down against a defense that has struggled to get off the field. Florida's road win at Texas was very real, but Georgia's front takes away the run game, and that's what made that upset possible. I'm taking Georgia to win the game 34-20. I think Florida did look really impressive on that road trip to Austin. They came home with a massive souvenir, but this is a different animal. Georgia now will be healthy coming out of the bye, and I think they've been excited about this opportunity to host this game in Atlanta." Georgia and Florida usually play in Jacksonville, but they're set to play in Atlanta this season (and in Tampa next season) due to renovations at EverBank Stadium. home.headline: Georgia’s new practice routine has made two Bulldogs’ injury status unknown
home.source: Dawn of the Dawg on MSN
home.blurb: Kirby Smart detailed on Monday how Georgia handled their bye week differently this season. In the past they have continued to practice like normal with limited time off, but this year they only practiced on Tuesday and Thursday and had the rest of the week off. "Really don't know on either one of them because we haven't done anything since Thursday,” Kirby Smart said via 247Sports.com . “Those guys, we had good practices all week last week, and then leading into this week, we'll find out more about where they are today and through the injury report information we have.” Smart made it clear that he is willing to sacrifice some practice time to get his team healthy. In fact, this is something that Georgia has been doing all season because they have shortened each of their practices all season by 10 or 15 minutes. The goal in this is to help Georgia stay healthier without giving up too much preparation time, and so far it has worked out alright. The hope though is that guys like Isiah Canion and KJ Bolden could use this extra time off this week to get healthy so they can make their return against Florida this weekend, but Smart hasn't confirmed if they will be back yet or not. The hope is that this would help get Georgia as healthy as possible going into the rest of the season, but according to Smart on Monday it still isn't clear if wide receiver Isiah Canion or defensive back KJ Bolden will be healthy enough to play against Florida this weekend. Georgia’s new practice routine will hopefully pay off Georgia is 6-1 so they could be better off this season, but their record is still good enough to be the No. 3 team in the country. UGA has also had to deal with a handful of injuries throughout the season, but if you compare their injury report to other teams across the country they have had less injuries than others. Georgia desperately needs KJ Bolden back Georgia has only been without KJ Bolden for one game this season, and it just so happened to be their worst game of the year. UGA was without Bolden when they played Auburn two weeks ago and they were upset at home as the No. 1 team in the country. Who knows if Bolden could've changed that outcome if he was in the game, but it might not be a coincidence that Georgia's defense had their worst game of the season when he wasn't able to play. Georgia has been without Canion for longer, so they've already learned how to get by without him on offense. The same can't be said for Bolden though who is a projected first round pick at the upcoming NFL Draft this offseason. If Georgia wants their best shot at avoiding another upset they need Bolden back in the lineup to help slow down a Florida offense who is capable of scoring a lot of points. Georgia fans face the terrifying prospect of a Saturday without football Kirby Smart leaves Georgia fans guessing with latest KJ Bolden update Georgia vs Florida opening spread won't make UGA feel any more comfortable Georgia vs Florida location change could benefit UGA

Georgia Football coach Kirby Smart Responded When Asked About Injuries to KJ Bolden and Isiah Canion Skip to main content SI.COM ATHENS - Georgia football coach Kirby Smart responded to a reporter’s question Monday about the status of two Bulldogs that missed the Auburn game a week ago. WR Isiah Canion and DB KJ Bolden both missed the the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry. Canion, who announced his transfer to Georgia from rival Georgia Tech in early January, has not played since the Bulldogs’ second game of the season against Western Kentucky. On the season Canion has three receptions for 28 yards total. Bolden has been a starting safety for the Bulldogs for most of his three-year career in Athens. Smart said after the Auburn game that Bolden just was not able to play. “KJ's been really good for us back there because he's a little bit of an eraser,” Smart said. “But that doesn't matter. At the end of the day, we have to go play with the guys we’ve got.” Smart was asked for an update on both Canion and Bolden on Monday - only a few days before the Bulldogs take on Florida in Atlanta. The SEC mandates that schools give an official injury report each Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday before conference games. The policy was put in place a few seasons ago to curb what conference members saw as a concern as gamblers taking advantage of so-called “inside information” to place bets on teams - and therefore players and staff being pressured to supply that information. Smart said he has be wary of the Dawgs’ injury situation as the season has grown longer. “I certainly hope we can manage the coming weeks with our players’ health well. It seems that we’re more beat up than we’ve been in the past when I send in injury reports,” Smart said last Tuesday. “That’s not because we’re doing more. picks.blurb: Previewing Northwestern's Upcoming Matchup Against Oregon as They Prepare to Face Another Tough Test on the Road Skip to main content SI.COM Olympic Sports More from Northwestern Wildcats On SI FOOTBALL The Wildcats hit the road once again, this time traveling west to Eugene, Oregon, for a Big Ten showdown against the Oregon Ducks on Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT. Oregon enters Saturday’s matchup looking to bounce back following a 21-10 loss to Illinois. The Ducks have been without starting quarterback Dante Moore for the past three games, and recent reports indicate he is unlikely to return this season after suffering a concussion earlier this year against USC. Oregon now sits at 10th in the conference with a 4-3 overall record this season. Meanwhile, the Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup fresh off a commanding 42-14 home victory over Rutgers, a win that propelled Northwestern to No. 20 in the AP Poll. A familiar face will return to Eugene this weekend, as former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly will take on the Ducks, this time as the Wildcats’ offensive coordinator. Under Kelly’s leadership, Northwestern’s offense has emerged as one of the best in the Big Ten this season, ranking third in the conference in total yards and points per game and second in rushing yards per game. The Wildcats head to Eugene looking to build on their success on both sides of the ball and extend their four-game winning streak. A major contributor to Northwestern’s offensive success this season has been quarterback Aidan Chiles, this week’s Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week, who has thrown for over 1,600 yards and 12 touchdowns, while recording just one interception. Chiles was dominant last time out against Rutgers, throwing for 219 yards and passing for three touchdowns, while rushing for 83 yards and two touchdowns. Komolafe delivered an especially impressive performance against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Wildcats’ convincing victory. Defensively, Northwestern has remained stout this season, spearheaded by defensive back Robert Fitzgerald and line backer Braydon Brus. Despite missing the last two games due to injury, Fitzgerald has recorded 49 tackles and two interceptions this season. The defensive back leads the Big Ten in tackles per game with nine, followed closely by Brus in second with 8.9. Brus leads the defensive unit with 62 tackles and has also notched an interception and fumble recovery this season. picks.headline: 4 bold predictions as Oregon football takes on Northwestern
picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL 4 bold predictions as Oregon football takes on Northwestern Alec Dietz Eugene Register-Guard Oct. 28, 2026, 8:52 a.m. PT Oregon's national-title hopes have ended after a loss to Illinois dropped them to 4-3. Oregon will face a one-loss Northwestern team featuring former Ducks coach Chip Kelly as offensive coordinator. The Ducks' defense is expected to play well, but the offense faces a tough challenge against Northwestern. The Oregon football team's national title hopes are all but over, and it isn't even November. After entering the season ranked as high as they've ever been, the Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) are unranked and out of the immediate College Football Playoff race after a stunning loss to Illinois on the road . The Ducks don't have much time to lick their wounds, either. After firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer and announcing quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the 2026 season , one-loss Northwestern comes to town . Chip Kelly, who guided Oregon to a national championship game appearance as head coach over a decade ago, is the Wildcats' offensive coordinator. "It's almost like you're playing three different offenses," Oregon coach Dan Lanning said of Northwestern. "The new wrinkles that (Kelly) has at Northwestern, some of the old flavor that he has that he's carried all the way to his time back here at Oregon. There's always going to be something new when you walk into a game that it's going to be like he's never put this on film. He might not know how you're going to line up against it, and you have to figure it out there within the rules of your defense and how you execute." Oregon vs. Northwestern scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks will have the home crowd behind them in Eugene and also have deep familiarity with Northwestern's starting quarterback, Aidan Chiles. The senior signal-caller started his career at Oregon State before transferring to Michigan State in 2024. Chiles played at Autzen Stadium in that year and had a rough outing, completely just 10 of 17 passes for 154 yards in a 31-10 loss. The Ducks found ways to rattle Chiles early, and with a strong pass rush in recent weeks they could do so again Saturday. Why Northwestern has an advantage: The Wildcats, under first-year offensive coordinator and former Ducks coach Chip Kelly, have one of the most efficient offenses in the country and don't make many mistakes. Northwestern isn't necessarily an offensive juggernaut, but it ranks fifth in the country in turnover margin and moves the ball methodically while keeping opposing teams out of the end zone defensively. Though the Wildcats' defense gives up plenty of yards, they rank in the top 25 in scoring defense allowing just 16.6 points per game. Oregon vs. Northwestern injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports were made public. For Oregon: The Ducks will have a good chunk of playmakers returning to the sideline this weekend after sitting out last week due to unknown reasons. Evan Stewart, who was out last week after a DUII arrest, is expected back, as are Jalen Lott and Messiah Hampton. Lanning did not elaborate why Hampton and Lott missed last week. The coach also announced quarterback Dante Moore will likely miss the rest of the 2026 season after sustaining a concussion in late September. For Northwestern: The Wildcats were without several key contributors last week in a win against Rutgers, especially defensively. Second-leading tackler Robert Fitzgerald was held out, as well as defensive lineman Brendan Flakes. Oregon vs. Northwestern: 4 bold predictions Ducks will mostly contain vaunted Northwestern run game Though Chiles has been successful through the air in recent weeks, Northwestern's bread and butter is establishing the ground game. After a subpar performance stopping the run last week against Illinois, Oregon's defense will show up ready to play and stifle backs Caleb Komolafe, Joseph Himon II and Gavin Sawchuk. Outside of games versus Oklahoma State and Illinois, Oregon's run defense has been sound and it'll look like a motivated group against a physical Wildcats team this weekend. Gage Hurych will have a bounce-back performance vs. Wildcats After missing three field goals last week in a loss to Illinois, all from 40 yards or more, junior kicker Gage Hurych will have a strong game against Northwestern. The Wildcats give up a lot of yards with a bend-but-don't-break defense but are elite in the red zone, an area where Oregon's offense struggles. Northwestern opponents only score a touchdown on 40% of possessions that reach the red zone. If Oregon's offense stalls as it gets closer to the end zone, look for Hurych to have a bounce-back performance with more manageable field-goal attempts. Ducks' defense will keep them in it until the end Though Oregon's offense will likely still have trouble after firing Drew Mehringer, its defense will respond and keep them in the game until the fourth quarter. Outside of a couple of broken off runs in a loss to Illinois, the Ducks' defense has been one of the top units in the country over the last month and that will continue against Northwestern this weekend. It just won't be enough to get a win, unless the offense really corrects itself. picks.headline: Northwestern is up next for Oregon football. A sneak preview
picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Northwestern is up next for Oregon football. A sneak preview Chris Hansen Eugene Register-Guard Oct. 26, 2026, 5:14 a.m. PT The Oregon Ducks will host the No. 18 Northwestern Wildcats on Saturday, October 31. Northwestern's offense is led by former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly, who is now the offensive coordinator. Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles is having a career-best season under Kelly's guidance. No time to wallow for Oregon's coaches and players. There's still lots of football left and against some pretty good teams. That includes this coming weekend. The Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten Conference) will host No. 18 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1) and former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly at 12:30 p.m. Oct. 31. Kelly, who is in his first season as offensive coordinator on coach David Braun's staff, has the Wildcats humming. They are third in the Big Ten in total yards per game (435.6) and points (34.7) and are No. 2 in rushing yards per game (204.6). Northwestern is coming off a 42-14 win against Rutgers, the fourth straight win for the Wildcats since a 29-23 loss to Indiana on Sept. 25. The Ducks are coming off a 21-10 loss to Illinois that, barring a miracle, has ended their shot at making the College Football Playoff for a third straight season. On Sunday, Oregon fired first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . Here's an early look at Northwestern. Who is the Northwestern QB? The Wildcats have a familiar face at quarterback in Aidan Chiles, who previously played at Oregon State and Michigan State. The 6-foot-4, 225-pound dual-threat senior has been unlocked by Kelly and is having the best season of his career. Chiles has completed 117 of 164 passes for 1,617 yards and has 12 touchdowns to one interception. He's also rushed for a team-leading nine touchdowns. Last week against Rutgers he completed 19 of 25 passes for 219 yards and three touchdowns and rushed for 83 yards and two touchdowns. He is the only player in the country to have multiple games of at least three passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns this season. Other Northwestern offensive standouts Junior wide receiver Griffin Wilde has 39 catches for 615 yards and four touchdowns. In the game against Rutgers on Saturday, he had nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown. Running back Caleb Komolafe leads the Wildcats in rushing with 551 yards and five touchdowns on 88 carries. He also had a big game against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown on just 13 carries (11.5 yards per run). Joseph Himon II has been productive as well. He has 371 yards and three scores on 38 carries with an average of 9.8 yards per run. Defensive standouts for Northwestern Fifth-year Braydon Brus has been disruptive from his linebacker position, leading the team with 62 tackles, 11.0 tackles for loss and four sacks. He also has an interception and a fumble recovery. He is the conference co-leader in tackles and No. 2 in TFLs. Safety Robert Fitzgerald, a second-team all-conference player in 2025, is second on the team with 49 tackles and has a team-leading two interceptions, though he has missed the last two games with an injury. Fitzgerald’s 9.0 tackles per game leads the Big Ten. The last time the Ducks and Wildcats met Oregon and Northwestern have played each other just two times, and never before at Autzen Stadium. The Wildcats beat the Ducks in Evanston, Ill., in 1974, and last season Oregon came out on top 34-14. Dante Moore was 16-of-20 passing for 178 yards and a touchdown, and Dierre Hill Jr. had a 66-yard touchdown run in the third quarter as the Ducks built a 31-0 lead. All of Northwestern's points came in the fourth quarter after the Ducks pulled most of their starters. away.blurb: Northwestern Legend Set to Return as Honorary Captain Against Rutgers NorthwesternRoundtable 102 Members • 1,228 Posts NorthwesternRoundtable NorthwesternRoundtable Related stories David Banks-Imagn Images David Banks-Imagn Images Northwestern Legend Set to Return as Honorary Captain Against Rutgers Alex Kwiatkowski Partner Oct 23, 2026 2:30 PM Published Oct 23, 2026 2:30 PM Former Northwestern quarterback and two-time Big Ten champion Steve Schnur will return as honorary captain against Rutgers, connecting the Wildcats' historic past with their promising 2026 season. Northwestern football is preparing for another important Big Ten matchup this weekend, but Saturday will also feature the return of one of the greatest quarterbacks in program history. Now, nearly three decades later, Schnur will return to Evanston as Northwestern looks to continue its impressive 2026 season. For players like Aidan Chiles and the rest of the roster, his return can serve as a reminder of what is possible when a team believes in itself and continues to work toward something bigger. And while this year’s Wildcats still have a long way to go, having a former player like Schnur return is a great way to connect the program’s successful past with its promising future. After all, years from now, some of these Wildcats could have the opportunity to return to Evanston and receive similar recognition for their own accomplishments. Former Wildcats quarterback Steve Schnur, a two-time Big Ten champion who helped lead Northwestern to the Rose Bowl, will serve as the team’s honorary captain against Rutgers at New Ryan Field. And for a program with such a memorable history, it’s a pretty special moment. Schnur played a major role in one of the most successful periods in Northwestern football history, helping the Wildcats capture back-to-back Big Ten championships in 1995 and 1996. During the 1995 season, Northwestern shocked the college football world by finishing the regular season 10-1 and earning its first Rose Bowl appearance since 1949. Schnur returned the following season and helped lead the Wildcats to another conference championship, earning first-team All-Big Ten honors in 1996. He finished his Northwestern career with 5,612 passing yards and 32 passing touchdowns while compiling a 19-8 record as the team’s starting quarterback. His accomplishments helped establish a new standard for Northwestern football and proved that the Wildcats could compete with some of the biggest programs in the country. And what makes this moment particularly special is the opportunity for the current players to share the field with someone who helped shape the program’s history. Schnur knows exactly what it takes to win at Northwestern, having experienced the challenges of building a successful program before helping lead the Wildcats to national prominence. away.blurb: EVANSTON, Ill. (AP) — Rutgers starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan left Saturday's 42-14 loss at No. 24 Northwestern and did not return after sustaining a blow to the head 6 minutes, 25 seconds into the first quarter. Scarlet Knights coach Greg Schiano told a Peacock sideline reporter at halftime that Lonergan was ruled out for the remainder to the game, but didn't elaborate on QB's condition. Lonergan was also injured late in Rutgers' season-opener against UMass on Sept. 3, then sat out a contest at Boston College on Sept. 11. He exited a home game against Indiana on Oct. 3 in the second quarter with an apparent head injury. Lonergan jogged a couple of sprints on the sidelines, but did not attempt a return. On the Scarlet Knights' first drive against Northwestern, Lonergan scrambled up the middle for a 5-yard gain, then slid forward to the ground at the Rutgers 45 with two Wildcats defenders closing in. Lonergan's momentum was finally stopped by Northwestern's Kobie McKinzie as the two players' helmets struck each other. Lonergan remained down on the field for a couple of minutes, then was helped by staff to a medical tent. The senior was replaced by junior AJ Surace, who led a drive for a field goal. home.headline: What we're hearing on Oregon injuries ahead of Illinois
home.blurb: While the Big Ten Availability report was released on Wednesday and will again come out on Thursday and Friday nights, we've got some intel on where things stand with each injured player and whether or not they will be able to contribute this weekend. Here's our early look at who we think could potentially be out or limited in this game on Saturday afternoon. After another week of practice, Dante Moore is still not ready to return to the field for the Ducks . It's been almost a month since his concussion vs. USC, so there is hope that he can return to play soon for Oregon, but the team continues to play it safe. There should be some real optimism that he can get back into the swing of things a week from now. Evan Stewart missed last week's game with an undisclosed injury, and then went on to get arrested on suspicion of a DUII later that night after the Ducks' win over Nebraska. Dan Lanning says that Stewart's situation will be handled internally, so there is no indication whether or not him being ruled out for this week's game is due to injury or discipline, but regardless of the reasoning, we will not see Stewart on Saturday. McClellan has been out for a few weeks now after suffering a broken foot in warmups before the Portland State game, abut for the first time since his injury, we saw him without a walking boon on Saturday night against Nebraska. There's a good chance that he returns to practice soon and get back on the field sometime next month for the Ducks. "He's going to be done for the foreseeable future. (It's) something he tried to tough out. You know, credit to him. Sometimes you can play through that, but you're probably not going to play as well. But it's one of those ones where it made sense to get it repaired for him." According to head coach Dan Lanning, Platt is still dealing with an undisclosed injury that held him out of the spring game earlier this year. Oregon's coach does not expect him to return to the field anytime soon. "He's gonna be limited for a while with the injury he felt in the spring," Lanning said of Platt. "I don't want to put a timeline on it, but he's going to be out for some time until we see where he's at and continue to progress and challenge himself." After suffering a neck injury during fall camp a year ago, Gresham was held out for the entire 2025 season and has yet to return to the field. Wide receiver Nyck Harbor is a big-play threat at any moment. Defensively, Dylan Stewart wreaks havoc on most offenses he faces — he's recorded two sacks and forced three fumbles in four games this season. home.headline: Oklahoma OT Michael Fasusi Expected to Return Against Mississippi State
home.blurb: Michael Fasusi was not listed on the final availability report ahead of OU's matchup against Mississippi State . He is projected to return to his starting spot at left tackle. The talented left tackle, who has missed every game since the Sooners' opener against UTEP, where he played only 17 snaps on offense per Pro Football Focus, was replaced by Ryan Fodje in OU's second game against Michigan. Fodje held the position over the next few weeks until his injury in last week's loss to Kentucky. Fodje is listed as out for today's game. Fasusi was initially listed as questionable on the SEC availability report on Wednesday. He was never upgraded on the Thursday and Friday reports. Eddy Pierre-Louis , a captain and starting left guard, has been out since appearing on the SEC availability report the week of the Texas game. He was in a cast on his right leg and used a single walking crutch. Pierre-Louis also missed last week's game against Kentucky and is out for today's game. Guard Heath Ozaeta was also not listed on the final availability report heading into the game with Mississippi State , meaning he will be available for the contest. Ozaeta appeared to injure his ankle during pregame warm-ups at the Cotton Bowl, but was able to play the entire game. Ozaeta missed last week and has been listed as questionable on this week's SEC availability reports. If he's available, he is projected to start at right guard. He has slowly ramped up his availability over the last few weeks as he deals with a right shoulder injury. In that game against UTEP, Fasusi was visibly dealing with the injury he sustained in Fall Camp. In his 17 offensive snaps, Fasusi was unable to lift or use his right arm in his final opportunities. Fasusi is a welcome addition to a depleted unit that has regressed both due to injuries and a lack of development. Fasusi could play alongside Noah Best , Jake Maikkula , and E'Marion Harris . If Ozaeta is unable to finish the game, he could be replaced by Peyton Joseph, who logged 69 offensive snaps in his first start of the season at right guard last week. home.blurb: Offensive linemen Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta and defensive back Eli Bowen were all listed as questionable on Friday night. Getting Fasusi and Ozaeta back would be a big boost for the o-line, while a return for Bowen would put the secondary back nearer to full strength than its been in weeks. That trio will be the players to watch on the final injury report on Saturday. The good news for the Sooners is that running back Tory Blaylock and wide receiver Parker Livingstone are off the injury report and therefore available to play in Starkville this week. Blaylock's return gives the Sooners a three-man rotation in the backfield again, while Livingstone's return gives them another option in the passing game. However, the Sooners also downgraded wide receiver Elijah Thomas to doubtful on Friday, meaning he likely won't face the Bulldogs. Running back Xavier Robinson will be out once again, as he was downgraded from doubtful to out. Along with Robinson, the Sooners will also not have wide receiver Trell Harris, tight end Trynae Washington, offensive linemen Eddy Pierre-Louis and Ryan Fodje, linebacker Taylor Heim, and defensive back Jacobe Johnson on Saturday. For Mississippi State, they got good news with the return of star running back Fluff Bothwell, who is off the injury report and is expected to play. According to multiple reports , star quarterback Kamario Taylor is also going to play this week, despite still being listed as questionable on Friday night's report. That means the Bulldogs will be getting their two best players back on the offensive side of the ball for Saturday's game. However, MSU will not have safety Issac Smith, which will be a big blow to their defense this week. Here's a look at Friday night's full injury report. home.blurb: Oklahoma leads SEC in players out, doubtful or questionable on Thursday injury report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF TRADE DEADLINE: Colts WR Josh Downs reportedly wants out amid fire sale As of Wednesday's initial report, the Sooners had more players out, doubtful and questionable -- 13 -- than any other SEC team. Vanderbilt had 11 and Ole Miss and Alabama had 10 on those lists. On Thursday, it wasn't much better. Oklahoma had 11 players listed as out, doubtful or questionable. Ole Miss had 10 and Alabama, Mississippi State and Vanderbilt had nine. The issue is particularly alarming on the Sooners' offensive line. As of Thursday, Eddy Pierre-Louis and Ryan Fodje were listed as out and Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta were listed as questionable. That report did not include Sean Hutton, who reportedly was transported to a local hospital Wednesday after suffering a non-contact injury . The receiver position has been hit hard, too. Trell Harris is out, and Elijah Thomas is questionable. Parker Livingstone has been upgraded to probable. Even coach Brent Venables has been out of action. He was ill and missed this week's media session. MORE: Oklahoma assistants Arbuckle, Bedenbaugh running out of time to fix offense Oklahoma offensive line coach Bedenbaugh's unit gets called out TRENDING Rays rally, avoid sweep Cliff Brunt Thu, October 22, 2026 at 7:47 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Oklahoma's Southeastern Conference injury report looks like a mini roster. The injury barrage is a key reason the Sooners are just 3-3 heading into Saturday's game at Mississippi State. Venables has been asked about the injuries several times this season. "I don't track what we what we do compared to other people," he said during the week before last Saturday's loss to Kentucky. "Certainly, you're always aware that injuries are part of game, and it's a physical, violent game." Venables said the team has to practice hard to be successful, so tapering back to avoid injury is not an option. "If you're casual at practice, you don't strain to finish at practice, all of those habits, good or bad, are going to show up," he said. "There's always a fine line. We've got to keep a healthy team, but we're very mindful of the time we put on the field, wear our GPS stuff, we look at all those types of things as well." Venables said much of the issue is coincidental, and he doesn't think there's anything fundamentally wrong with the way the team prepares. "We're not doing things different from how I've done it for a long time, whether I was an assistant or not," he said. "We have to practice the right way, though."
