home.headline: Oklahoma vs. Mississippi State injury report: Who's out and who has to step up for the Sooners
home.blurb: Oklahoma vs. Mississippi State injury report: Who's out and who has to step up for the Sooners Skip to main content Recruiting Mississippi State star quarterback Kamario Taylor was listed as questionable all week leading up to the Bulldogs hosting OU at 2:30 p.m. CT Saturday in Starkville, but the final availability report just ahead of kickoff revealed that he'll actually be available. That still doesn't mean Taylor will be 100%, though. Taylor has emerged as a Heisman Trophy contender this season as, statistically, the best quarterback in the SEC. There's doubt that the Bulldogs are a tier lower without him on the field. Mississippi State was shut out by LSU 31-0 last week with Taylor on the sideline because of turf toe. Before getting blanked, the Bulldogs had averaged 39 points per game. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas was rolled up on in the second quarter against Kentucky last week and never returned. That will cost him a game after being downgraded to doubtful on Friday's availability report, then finally to out on Saturday. He has five catches for 49 yards this season after getting a bigger role since Trell Harris' injury. Replacement: This should open up even more opportunities for Manny Choice, who signed with Thomas in the 2025 class, after he broke out last week and led the Sooners with 98 receiving yards against Kentucky. With or without Thomas, Choice has earned a role as WR2 behind Isaiah Sategna. Ryan Fodje was clearly hurt near the end of last week's game against Kentucky before finally coming out. He was then immediately listed as out on the initial availability report. Fodje also missed the season opener, but had started every game since at left tackle to replace Michael Fasusi. Obviously, the Sooners are thin at tackle, and with Eddy Pierre-Louis out for the third straight game, they have the same problem at guard, especially with Heath Ozaeta also banged up. Pierre-Louis started the first three games of the season at left guard before losing that job to Ozaeta, then ultimately getting sidelined. Ozaeta was questionable to miss a second straight game and possibly leave the Sooners dangerously thin at guard. He was OU's only reliable depth piece with experience before he cracked the starting lineup again, and now that he's healthy, he'll start again. Replacement: Joseph started at right guard opposite freshman Noah Best last week with Pierre-Louis and Ozaeta out. Since Ozaeta and Fasusi are both available, Joseph can now be a rotational player at both spots. Fasusi's return is the Sooners' greatest blessing after being sidelined since he injured his shoulder in the first quarter of OU's season opener. He's not only OU's best offensive lineman, but he also frees up more options elsewhere up front and gives the Sooners options behind the starting group. Replacement: Fodje had been filling in for Fasusi, but obviously that can't happen this week, so this return couldn't have come at a better time. LB Jalen Smith: out S Isaac Smith: ou

picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 3-2 ACC) is coming off a last-minute 20-16 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies at Memorial Stadium. The Tigers led for much of the second half, but Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led his team on an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning score with 1:44 to play. Grunkmeyer's 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth-and-1 gave Virginia Tech its first win over Clemson in 19 years and dropped the Tigers to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. The offense struggled once again, netting only 288 total yards and going 3 of 14 on third downs. Freshman QB Tait Reynolds completed 20 of his 26 passes, but his average completion went for only 5.9 yards. The Tigers rank dead last in the ACC and just 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game. Clemson will face a Florida State (3-4, 1-3) team fresh off a bye, and one that should be playing with plenty of confidence. Mike Norvell's Seminoles took the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes into double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 17. Fifth-year senior Ashton Daniels leads the Seminoles' passing attack and has 1,618 yards and 12 touchdowns to eight interceptions in seven games this season. Daniels threw four touchdown passes and rushed for another score in FSU's loss to Miami in Week 7. Clemson has won nine of the last 10 meetings against Florida State dating back to 2015. It gives Florida State a 71.9% chance to win and Clemson a 28.1% chance. The Tigers are 51st nationally in ESPN's FPI with a 5.8 rating, which ranks 11th among the 17 ACC teams. picks.blurb: Early odds for Florida State vs. Clemson in Week 9 show what standing with Miami can do Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's basketball Women's basketball Baseball & softball FanSided NCAA Sites After battling through injuries and adversity against Miami in Week 7, Florida State must now return to the playing field against the Clemson Tigers. Week 7 was exhausting for everyone, between the gritty battle on the field, the two ridiculous calls, and the season-ending injury to star running back Ousmane Kromah. Even with a bye in Week 8, the tension from the previous weeks feels like it is lingering, and the Seminoles now need to get back into the win column. Florida State's first opponent after the bye week will be Clemson, a team sitting in a very similar position with little success on the field despite very high expectations. Coach Mike Norvell is going to be sticking around Tallahassee for a bit longer, and losing to Clemson directly after that announcement became public would be an awful look. Norvell may not have secured the win in Coral Gables, but taking Miami into double overtime appears to have been enough to win back the trust of the public. After previously hosting Virginia this season as underdogs, Florida State is a home favorite for the first time since hosting Central Arkansas earlier in the year. The Seminoles should be favorites at home games with the crowd that the team can bring in, but, notably, Florida State is a heavier moneyline favorite than normal. The last time Florida State played at home this season, Virginia was considered to be the favorite despite being the visiting team. The Seminoles impressed with a dominant win, but now the team needs to same result on the field with the public backing them this time. There is enough evidence to suggest this can be a strong team, but consistency has been the problem the Seminoles cannot shake. Clemson is not coming into the game as the hottest team either, which could factor into the support for Florida State. The Tigers are 4-3, and with no real solution at quarterback, the team does not look like one that can muster up enough offense to beat opponents. Clemson has scored 29 points in the last two ACC games against Virginia Tech and Miami after posting 52 in the first two conference games. The Tigers averaged 4.6 yards per play during the 41-13 loss to Miami, with quarterback Tait Reynolds turning the ball over twice. The offense managed to move the ball against a solid Virginia Tech defense, but the team still only put together a 16-point performance, which will not be enough to defeat Florida State. Losing to Miami definitely stings, but the reality is that the ACC as a whole is not that great this season outside of the Hurricanes, SMU, and Wake Forest. Florida State could definitely take advantage of that moving forward with similar performances on offense to the one that brought the team into double overtime. away.headline: Mike Norvell discusses FSU football's must-win game vs Clemson
away.blurb: News Sports Restaurants Real Estate Opinion Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Mike Norvell discusses FSU football's must-win game vs Clemson Peter Holland Jr. Tallahassee Democrat Oct. 28, 2026, 10:30 a.m. ET With Florida State’s Halloween showdown against Clemson just days away, coach Mike Norvell returns to the podium Wednesday as the Seminoles prepare for a pivotal ACC matchup. Seeking to snap a two-game losing streak, FSU is looking to regain momentum and keep its postseason goals within reach. The Seminoles (3-4, 1-2 ACC) have not played since a double-overtime loss to now-No. 1 Miami on Oct. 17, making the bye week a critical opportunity to regroup. At 3-4, FlSU needs a win to move back within one game of .500 before consecutive ACC road trips to Boston College and Pittsburgh. With pressure mounting on Norvell and little margin for error the rest of the season, the matchup against Clemson (4-3, 2-2) carries significant weight. Follow along for live updates from Norvell's Wednesday press conference. away.headline: DT Vic Burley added to injury report for Clemson vs Virginia Tech
away.blurb: TRADE DEADLINE: Colts WR Josh Downs reportedly wants out amid fire sale Burley, a senior, was listed as questionable again after being added Oct. 22. He was not listed on the initial report Oct. 21. Burley has played in four games after missing the first two because of a suspension. He got his first tackle, a sack, in Week 7 vs Georgia Southern. Clemson wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. Christopher Vizzina injury update Swinney said backup quarterback Christopher Vizzina is having his "best week by far" of the season and that he's 90% healthy. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' And he's like, 'Let's put Brock in,'" Swinney said. "So that was really his call. Coach C.V." home.headline: Florida State injury updates: Mike Norvell expects key returns, but timing is an issue
home.blurb: Florida State coach Mike Norvell recently provided a couple of injury updates on multiple Seminoles who have missed significant time this season. Injuries have been a huge issue for the team this year for Norvell, particularly on defense, where multiple players are out for the season. Sometimes injuries can make or break a team, and so far, the Seminoles have been able to do quite a bit with multiple contributors sidelined. Norvell kicked off his injury updates portion of the press conference with a quick tidbit on linebacker Blake Nichelson, who has not played since the season opener against New Mexico State. Nichelson is nearing a return, and while the game against Clemson might still be out of reach , the linebacker should be able to return to play soon. Samuel Singleton Jr.'s return would be huge for the Florida State offense Norvell is not giving up on Singleton's return; he never ruled the running back out for the season, and he clearly still thinks there is hope for his return. It might be a delusion at this point from Norvell to avoid the reality that Florida State is in a bad spot at running back, or a future return this season might still truly be in the cards. I personally would like to think that Singleton is close to coming back, and the faster he can return, the better for Florida State. Tre Wisner is an experienced running back, but he has not been the most effective player in a short sample size this season. Aside from Wisner, there is not much of an experienced supporting cast. Additionally, Florida State might be in trouble if Singleton is not able to return this season due to the fact that there are only three healthy running backs. The Seminoles truly cannot afford to have another running back go down with an injury, and if Singleton is not available for another two or three weeks, that could be an issue. The timing of Crutchfield's return could not be any better, with Quindarrius Jones, Nehemiah Chandler, and Ashlynd Barker all dealing with injuries. Barker has been playing through his injury thanks to a cast, but Crutchfield can do it all in the secondary, and he should be able to take some pressure off multiple players. home.headline: Seminoles should be healthier after bye, but some injury concerns linger on defense
Florida State could receive a massive boost on defense with Blake Nichelson nearing a return
home.blurb: Florida State could receive a massive boost on defense with Blake Nichelson nearing a return Skip to main content Recruiting Coach Mike Norvell took the podium this afternoon following practice for his first press conference of the week, and some injury updates were provided. Norvell revealed that senior linebacker Blake Nichelson is "progressing" but likely still would not be able to return to play just yet. With Clemson coming to Tallahassee on October 31, Nichelson may need more time to properly rehab his injury. The linebacker recorded three total tackles against New Mexico State in the season opener in Tallahassee before going down with an injury. Nichelson has not seen the field since, but a return during the season has never been ruled out. Florida State could greatly benefit from a Blake Nichelson return this season Both for Nichelson and Florida State, returning to the field this season would be extremely beneficial, given the struggles the team has had. The Seminoles are down so many players at some positions that some players are playing significantly more than the staff would like. Nichelson gives the rest of the linebackers a chance to breathe, and he offers the staff a veteran presence that can help the defense work out some of the communication issues present. Florida State is right back into game mode after receiving a bye in Week 8 to recuperate for the final five games of the 2026 season. The year has been far from what the fans had hoped for, but unfortunately, it has been eerily similar to what many experts felt it would be. Once again, the Seminoles are in an awkward position as the light that comes with winning is slowly fading away. For the Seminoles, virtually the entire roster has been hit with injuries at one point or another this season, and some positions took big hits. The secondary has been running with nearly no depth due to the number of injuries, and other positions have been playing without key players for most of the season. At linebacker, Nichelson was expected to take another step forward this season for Florida State, with a bigger role on defense. However, Nichelson's injury forced the Seminoles' staff to move things around, and nearly every linebacker has been included in an injury report this season. The Seminoles need to get healthy to be more competitive this season, and getting Nichelson back would be a huge boost defensively. Nichelson has been a Florida State mainstay the past few seasons , with 115 total tackles since the 2023 season. Losing Nichelson so early on in the season was an unfortunate blow, as what should have been a breakout season for the linebacker has turned into a disappointing year. Norvell also provided a key update on defensive back Jordan Crutchfield, who should be in line to see the playing field this week against Clemson. You don't start 7-0, score nearly 50 points a game and climb to No. 1 by accident. But there's something about laying more than two touchdowns on the road that makes me uncomfortable, especially against a North Carolina team that's been hanging around with some decent opponents. Miami probably wins this game. I'd be surprised if it didn't. But asking the Hurricanes to go into Chapel Hill and win by 17? That's a different bet altogether. Be ready for all the college football action with our free college football picks . Miami heads to Kenan Memorial Stadium in Chapel Hill on Saturday, October 31, 2026. Kickoff is set for 7:30 PM ET on ABC. The Hurricanes opened as 14.5-point favorites, with some books now showing 15.5. Our original betting numbers were North Carolina +16.5 and Under 51.5. That extra point on the spread matters, and I wouldn't pretend every sportsbook is still offering it. This is an outdoor game, so I'll want another look at the Chapel Hill weather forecast before kickoff, particularly the wind and any chance of rain. Miami Hurricanes Have the Offense to Put This Away Early Miami is 7-0, including 3-0 away from home, and just beat Pittsburgh 52-23. The Hurricanes have scored 43 or more in three of their last four games, and they've already beaten Clemson 41-13 on the road. That's a pretty good argument for laying the points, I'll give you that. Pittsburgh couldn't do much with Miami's passing game Saturday. The Hurricanes scored 52, and the scary part is that they still left some plays out there. North Carolina isn't going to survive if it spends the first half giving Miami short fields and easy touchdowns. The numbers explain why the Hurricanes are such a big favorite. They're averaging 49 points and 552 yards per game. Nobody in the country is producing more total offense. Miami throws for about 341 yards a game and runs for another 211, so taking away one part of the offense doesn't necessarily solve anything. Defensively, the Hurricanes allow just 15.3 points and 60 rushing yards per game. Sixty. That's going to make life difficult for a North Carolina offense that hasn't run the ball particularly well. Miami also converts 54.5% of its third downs. If the Tar Heels can't get the Hurricanes off the field, that home crowd won't have much to cheer about. Sign Up Get $30 Premium Picks Credit + Exclusive Offers Darian Mensah is having one heck of a season. He's thrown for 2,151 yards with 22 touchdowns and just one interception, completing better than 81% of his passes. Against Pittsburgh, he went 31-for-37 for 387 yards and four scores. Malachi Toney caught 16 passes for 194 yards and three touchdowns in that game, giving him 952 receiving yards and 11 touchdowns on the season. Javian Mallory has added 444 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. That's plenty of offense for North Carolina to worry about. Miami does have some injuries, with receiver Jalen Moore and running back Chris Brown out for the season. Tight end Logan Gilbert is also sidelined, while Owen Ruskavich's status needs checking. But the Hurricanes haven't had much trouble scoring without them. North Carolina Tar Heels Need to Make Miami Earn Everything North Carolina is 4-3 overall and 1-2 at home. The Tar Heels had won two straight before losing 31-30 to Syracuse in overtime Saturday. That one had to sting. They had a chance to get their fifth win and instead let Syracuse walk out of Chapel Hill with it. Still, I wouldn't throw out everything North Carolina has done because of one ugly finish. The Tar Heels beat Pittsburgh 21-17 on the road and followed it with a 24-20 win at Duke. They also played Clemson to an eight-point game. Those aren't the results of a team that rolls over every time it sees a better opponent. The offense is the problem. North Carolina averages 24.4 points and 336 yards per game, and the running game produces only 114 yards a night. That's not much help against Miami's defensive front. The Tar Heels are probably going to have to throw more than they'd like. Defensively, though, they've allowed 20.9 points per game. That's respectable, even if the 373 yards they're giving up tells you opponents are moving the ball. What worries me most is third down. North Carolina allows opponents to convert 43.1% of the time. Miami is one of the best third-down teams in the country. That's a bad matchup, and Bill Belichick has to find a way to get his defense off the field before the Hurricanes start piling up possessions. Billy Edwards Jr. has thrown for 1,530 yards with 11 touchdowns and five interceptions. He passed for 271 yards and two scores against Syracuse, so he can move the ball when he gets protection. Jordan Shipp has 543 receiving yards, including eight catches for 102 yards and a touchdown Saturday. Benjamin Hall leads the running backs with 283 yards, while Demon June has seven rushing touchdowns. The Tar Heels are dealing with some injuries at receiver, including Carnell Warren and Kaden Chapman, and they're missing tight ends Jordan Washington and Jake Warren. That's not ideal when you're facing a defense as good as Miami's. But Edwards has enough experience to keep North Carolina from becoming completely one-dimensional. Miami vs North Carolina Picks and Predictions North Carolina Tar Heels +16.5 I'm taking North Carolina +16.5, assuming that number is still available. I know Miami could make this look foolish in a hurry. The Hurricanes have the better quarterback, the better offense and a defense that barely lets anybody run the ball. But sixteen and a half points is a lot to lay on the road against a team that's been competitive with Clemson, Pittsburgh and Duke. North Carolina has lost three games, and two of those defeats came by eight points or fewer. The Tar Heels also have a quarterback who can throw well enough to put together a late scoring drive if they're down a couple of touchdowns. That's what I'm looking for here. Miami can control most of the game and still fail to cover a number this big. I wouldn't be surprised by a 30-17 or 34-20 Miami win. Either one gets the job done for North Carolina backers at +16.5. At +14.5, though, I like it considerably less. I'll take Under 51.5, although this is the pick that makes me a little nervous. Miami is averaging 49 points a game by itself, and that's not something you can just ignore. But North Carolina isn't built to get into a scoring contest with the Hurricanes. The Tar Heels need to run some clock, avoid turnovers and make Miami work for its points. They can't afford to turn this into a game where both teams are snapping the ball every twenty seconds. Miami's defense should help us here because the Hurricanes allow only 15.3 points per game and have been excellent against the run. If North Carolina finishes somewhere around 14 or 17 points, Miami can score into the low 30s without pushing this over. The danger is an early Miami explosion or a couple of defensive touchdowns. That's real. But I think the Tar Heels will try to slow the game down, and Miami's defense should keep North Carolina from doing too much scoring. Give me Miami 31-17. Final Picks: North Carolina Tar Heels +16.5 and Under 51.5 Betting on College Football? away.headline: Notre Dame can survive its latest injury wave against Navy, but Miami is different
away.blurb: Notre Dame football’s “ next man up ” philosophy should be enough to get Marcus Freeman through Navy despite another crowded injury report. But with DJ McKinney out, Brauntae Johnson still sidelined, and Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa among the questionable players, Chris Ash needs that list to shrink considerably before Miami arrives. Despite the Fighting Irish coming off a bye week , head coach Marcus Freeman detailed several injuries that will hit Chris Ash’s unit hard. The good news is that none of the players who will miss time or be questionable are ones the team should need against Navy. The question is how healthy some of these guys will be in two weeks against Miami. On Monday afternoon, Freeman said McKinney is out for the Navy game with an ankle injury. That’s never good news, as that kind of injury can stick around for a while. A cornerback who can’t make cuts won’t keep up with receivers. That’s not an issue against Navy, but against Miami, especially Malachi Toney, it’s a big one. Another big injury update: safety Brauntae Johnson is still out. Notre Dame has hoped he’d be out for “just a couple of weeks” after he was injured in the first half of the season opener. However, with the season now in Week 8, people have to start worrying about whether he will play this year. The injury list doesn’t end there. Freeman said that tight end Cooper Flanagan (hamstring), linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa (thumb), defensive lineman Loghan Thomas (shoulder), and cornerback Mark Zackery IV (concussion) are all questionable. Of course, of all the injuries that might just be cautionary, KVA’s questionable status is the most likely situation where he could have been fine to play if Miami was this week. Notre Dame should absolutely be able to beat Navy even without Viliamu-Asa in the lineup. The injury that should make Notre Dame faithful most worried is DJ McKinney’s. The transfer cornerback was hurt late in the game against BYU , and the bye week apparently wasn't enough time for him to heal and get back to 100%. Notre Dame football defensive injuries create bigger questions for Miami than Navy Because Notre Dame knows Navy won’t tax its cornerbacks much, sitting McKinney this week isn’t a shock. It’s even possible that if this were Miami week , they’d be working to get him back on the field. The Irish won’t push it against the Midshipmen. The most interesting note in that group is that Notre Dame took quite a bit of heat for not playing Viliamu-Asa more against BYU. It’s clear now that one reason he wasn’t in the game more was that his thumb was still bothering him. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer return with their picks for the weekend's top games Getty Images Another weekend in college football , another carnage-filled Saturday. This feels like 2007 all over again, thanks to the pure chaos that has ensued over the last two weeks within the top 25. At this point, we're not expecting anything less on Halloween in Week 9, despite only two matchups pitting nationally ranked teams -- the SEC's Georgia vs. Florida showdown from Atlanta and Arizona vs. Texas Tech in the topsy-turvy Big 12. Only three unbeatens in the Power Four remain as the season approaches its final month, with the first CFP rankings set to debut in less than a week. We hope you're betting responsibly this fall, considering this parity-rich party nationwide that shows no signs of ceasing. Season results : Brad Crawford (47-24 straight up, 35-35-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (51-20 straight up, 38–32-1 ATS) My colleague's hot streak continues. After tying things up at midseason against the spread, Hummer's sizzling Week 8 effort has pushed him out front. It's quite humbling for yours truly, whose multi-year reign atop the picks mountain is in serious jeopardy. Perhaps Saturday afternoon comes up aces for me, and we enter November tied again after a rally. On the flip side, Hummer's could swell. No. 25 Wisconsin at Iowa (-3.5) Hummer ( Wisconsin +3.5) : These two teams do the same things well: Run the ball, stop the run. The Hawkeyes are a better rushing offense, while Wisconsin, with Colton Joseph , has the more dynamic option at quarterback -- he uses his legs a lot. To me, this game comes down to which team can avoid turnovers. They've been a killer in losses for Iowa this season. Iowa avoids those against the Badgers and wins a classic Big Ten slugfest at home. The Badgers cover, though. … Iowa 20, Wisconsin 17. Crawford (Wisconsin +3.5) : Had a feeling the Badgers would be ranked at some point this season after watching the opener against Notre Dame . The operation just looked more fluid, despite the final score in a matchup that was more competitive than the final outcome. I believe oddsmakers are giving too much respect to the Hawkeyes here playing at home. An outright win could move the Badgers inside the top 20 of the CFP selection committee's first rankings next week. I'll go ahead and take this one as my upset special in Week 9. ... Wisconsin 23, Iowa 20. No. 22 Arizona at No. 13 Texas Tech (-5.5) Hummer (Texas Tech -5.5 ): A critical matchup in the Big 12 race, the Red Raiders are facing their toughest test since Houston in Week 2. The Wildcats have put up points in bunches this season. But I will say the one week the Wildcats struggled was against BYU , when their run game was bottled up by BYU's defensive front. That's a major potential advantage for Texas Tech in this matchup. The Red Raiders are an excellent front seven and should win that matchup. Can Texas Tech score enough to win this one? It's been a struggle at times, but they get it done. … Texas Tech 27, Arizona 20. Crawford (Texas Tech -5.5) : This is the week we'll be talking about the Wildcats nationally if Arizona finds a way to beat Texas Tech in Lubbock. I don't think it happens, however. The Red Raiders' backs are against the wall in this spot, knowing another loss tanks any shot at reaching the CFP -- or even getting back to the Big 12 title game as the defending league champions. Will Hammond does not have a multi-touchdown outing this season as a passer, but this could be the weekend it finally happens at home. I trust Texas Tech more in this spot than Arizona. ... Texas Tech 31, Arizona 24. Auburn at No. 12 Ole Miss (-12.5) Hummer ( Auburn +12.5): Auburn has struggled this year against above-average defensive fronts. The Rebels aren't elite in that area, but they do blitz a ton and create a lot of havoc around the line of scrimmage. It's going to be up to Byrum Brown to pick up those blitzes and extend plays with his feet. Even without Kewan Lacy , Trinidad Chambliss allows them to score enough. The question is whether Auburn can keep up. I think the Tigers do enough to cover. … Ole Miss 34, Auburn 24. Crawford (Auburn +12.5) : Life in the SEC is hard. Auburn goes from beating Georgia in Athens one week to getting housed on The Plains by another nationally ranked foe the next. Rinse, repeat. If the Tigers had trouble defending Sam Leavitt and that LSU offense, they're going to have equally as much trouble this weekend in Oxford against Trinidad Chambliss. We've seemed to have dismissed his Heisman hopes after the loss at Texas , and that's unwise. Ole Miss gets Georgia coming up, and there are several more opportunities to shine, including this one. I do still have questions about this Ole Miss defense, however. ... Ole Miss 38, Auburn 27. Minnesota at No. 4 Indiana (-20.5) Hummer ( Minnesota +20.5) : That feels like an aggressive line based on what we've seen from Indiana 's offense of late, right? The Gophers are a top-30 defense in terms of yards allowed per play and should be able to challenge Indiana the way Nebraska , Ohio State and Michigan have in recent weeks. The question becomes, can Minnesota score enough to make this a game? The Gophers are 118th nationally in yards per play and have only scored more than 21 points against Power Four competition once this season. It's going to be tough for Minnesota to manufacture points, but the Gophers do enough. … Indiana 27, Minnesota 10. Crawford (Minnesota +20.5) : Can Indiana cover a three-touchdown spread? I have my doubts with Josh Hoover back there. Maybe this is the week the Hoosiers figure it out in the passing game, but the Gophers are sound on the back end and aren't likely to give up explosive plays. I've moved off Indiana in the elite tier of playoff contenders, but the Hoosiers should win here and be ranked inside the top 5 in next week's first CFP rankings. ... Indiana 31, Minnesota 17 . No. 17 Florida vs. No. 3 Georgia (-10.5) Hummer (Florida +10.5) : Was Florida's defensive performance against Texas an aberration or the new norm? That's the big question entering this game. The Gators are 121st nationally in passing yards per game, and the Bulldogs are a top-30 passing offense. That should be a big advantage for UGA. But that unit largely held Texas in check. Otherwise, this is a reasonably even matchup across the board. Georgia's O-line is better -- yes. Florida matches up well otherwise. Georgia wins this game coming off the bye week. But I do like the Gators to stay in this one for 60 minutes. … Georgia 34, Florida 27. Crawford (Georgia -10.5) : One of college football's most difficult teams to predict this season, I'm 0-2 picking the Gators against the spread after the loss to South Carolina and subsequent rally at Texas. I've given up trying to figure out which Florida team shows up week to week since that 4-0 start in September pushed the Gators to No. 8 in the AP poll. A victory in Atlanta puts Jon Sumrall's squad back in the CFP discussion near the top of the SEC and threatens Georgia's reign in the league standings. What's more likely, however, is Gunner Stockton recovering from his mistake-filled last outing and the Bulldogs shutting down the run. As of Tuesday, Sumrall hasn't named his starting quarterback, but I think the hotter hand -- Tramell Jones -- gives OC Buster Faulkner and the Gators the better shot here. ... Georgia 30, Florida 14. No. 6 Utah (-6.5) at Cincinnati Hummer ( Cincinnati +6.5) : On the right week, Cincinnati is capable of beating anyone in the Big 12. We just saw that against Texas Tech. But can the Bearcats do it two weeks in a row? It'll come down to the defense. That unit stepped up against the Red Raiders, holding them to 24 points. Can a unit that ranks 109th nationally in yards allowed per play do that twice in a row? I'm skeptical, especially given how good the Utes are up front. The good news for Cincinnati is its offensive line can match up with anyone. These two offensive fronts lean on each other, and the Utes pull away late. … Utah 24, Cincinnati 20. Crawford (Utah -6.5) : Could the Bearcats put it together in consecutive weeks against top-10 conference opponents? I'll lean no, but it'll be competitive. I was impressed with the Utes' performance last week against Houston, coming back from 10 points down to thwart the Cougars' road upset bid. Utah is now my projected favorite in the conference, and a win this weekend sets up fireworks against BYU on Nov. 7. Just don't get caught looking ahead in this trap spot. ... Utah 34, Cincinnati 24. After a bye week, the Buckeyes will now be facing off against the USC Trojans, giving this team another test to overcome. Ohio State remains one of the better teams in the country, but the Trojans will be a challenge. This will be the first game between the two historic programs in Big Ten play, giving each another reason to want to win. The two programs have met multiple times over the years, and it's always been a fun matchup. The Buckeyes did lose starting quarterback Julian Sayin, likely for the season, but this team still has a lot of talent on the roster. Ohio State believes that it can still win a title this season, and the Trojans are just the next team in its way. As the team gets ready for the Trojans, they will be entering the game with a record of 6-1, going 4-0 in Big Ten play. USC comes in with a record of 6-2, going 3-2 in their conference games so far. The Trojans are coming off a bad loss to the Wisconsin Badgers last weekend, giving this team all the desperation they need. The Buckeyes will need to stay focused in this game, looking at this trip as purely business. Entering the game, the Buckeyes are still favored to take down the Trojans, even with the injury to Sayin. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Ohio State has an 82.8 percent chance of defeating USC on the road this week. For the Buckeyes, making sure to keep the basics the same in this game will be a key. Even without Sayin, the offense should still run through star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, giving the team a boost. Ohio State may rely even more heavily on Smith to help whoever is under center for this Buckeyes team, giving them a reliable target. Smith is on pace for a truly special season, and the loss of Sayin shouldn't change that fact. The Buckeyes defense will also be tasked with slowing down USC quarterback Jayden Maiava, who has thrown for 2,302 yards with 19 touchdowns and five interceptions. The Trojans rely on their offense to set the tone for the team, and the defense has been a little shaky this season. Kickoff between the two sides is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT/7:30 p.m. ET from the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.

You don't lose a quarterback who's thrown 19 touchdown passes and just shrug it off. But I've got a question for anybody ready to jump on USC because of that injury. Did you watch what Wisconsin did to the Trojans last Saturday? USC couldn't run the ball, couldn't protect its quarterback, and scored seven points. Seven. Ohio State heads west to play USC at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on Saturday, October 31, 2026. Kickoff is at 7:30 PM ET on NBC. The Buckeyes opened as 6.5-point favorites, with the spread now around seven at several sportsbooks. Totals have been listed between 50.5 and 51.5, down from some earlier numbers. Rain is possible in Los Angeles on Saturday evening, although the forecast could change before kickoff. That would be one more thing for both offenses to deal with. Ohio State Buckeyes Have a Defense Worth Trusting Ohio State is 6-1 overall and 2-1 on the road. The Buckeyes had last weekend off after beating Indiana 19-15 on October 17. That wasn't a pretty win, and it certainly wasn't the offensive performance Ohio State fans are used to seeing. But they went into Bloomington and beat a good football team. Before that, they handled Maryland 45-16 and Iowa 31-14. Their only loss came by one point at Texas in the opener. I know everybody wants to talk about the quarterback injury. That's fair. But this team didn't suddenly forget how to play football because Sayin got hurt. Ohio State is averaging 39.3 points and 476 yards per game. The Buckeyes throw for 323 yards a night, although those passing numbers were built with Sayin running the offense. I wouldn't expect the same production immediately from a freshman quarterback. The defense is another story. Ohio State gives up only 13.4 points and 264 yards per game. Opponents are running for fewer than 93 yards a night. That's what makes this matchup interesting. USC just finished with minus-17 rushing yards against Wisconsin. If the Trojans can't run the ball Saturday, Ohio State can spend most of the night going after Jayden Maiava. And that could get ugly. Sign Up Get $30 Premium Picks Credit + Exclusive Offers Luke Fahey is expected to take over for Sayin, who suffered an arm injury against Indiana and is out for several weeks. Fahey has completed nine of 13 passes for 203 yards this season, with two touchdowns and two interceptions. That's not much experience, and his first start coming at the Coliseum isn't ideal. But he's got Jeremiah Smith to throw to. Smith has 984 receiving yards, and that's a pretty nice option for a young quarterback trying to settle down. Bo Jackson leads the Buckeyes with 516 rushing yards, although he's been dealing with a shoulder injury. Austin Siereveld and Kenyatta Jackson have also had injury concerns. Ohio State needs to check those boxes before Saturday, but I expect Ryan Day to keep the offense fairly simple early and let the defense do its job. USC Trojans Need to Protect Their Quarterback USC is 6-2 overall and 4-0 at home. The Trojans were looking pretty good before heading to Wisconsin last weekend. They'd beaten Penn State and Washington, and Lincoln Riley's offense was putting points on the board. Then Wisconsin beat them 24-7, and it wasn't particularly close once the Badgers took control in the second half. USC finished with 241 total yards and gave up five sacks. The Trojans also turned the ball over twice in the first half. That's a bad afternoon for anybody, but it's especially troubling when Ohio State is the next team on the schedule. USC averages 32.8 points and 435 yards per game. The passing game produces better than 303 yards a night, so there's no shortage of talent on offense. The trouble is getting enough help from the running game. USC averages only 131 rushing yards, and Wisconsin showed what happens when that part of the offense disappears completely. The Trojans were stuck throwing the ball, and the Badgers knew it. USC's defense allows 25 points and 331 yards per game, including 216 through the air. Those aren't terrible numbers, but they're not exactly the kind that make me think Ohio State's freshman quarterback is going to have nowhere to throw. The Trojans need to get pressure on Fahey without leaving Smith running free downfield. Maiava has thrown for 2,303 yards with 19 touchdowns and five interceptions. He's been good for most of the season, but those two interceptions against Wisconsin hurt. King Miller has 602 rushing yards and four touchdowns, although he managed only eight yards on 11 carries Saturday. That's not going to work against Ohio State. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt leads the receivers with 400 yards, while Trent Mosley has 411 yards and five touchdowns. There's enough talent for USC to score, but the offensive line has to give those guys a chance. Maiava was sacked five times against Wisconsin. If that happens again, I don't care how many good receivers the Trojans have. They're going to struggle to move the ball. Ohio State vs USC Picks and Predictions Ohio State Buckeyes -6.5 I'm taking Ohio State -6.5. I know the quarterback situation makes this a little uncomfortable, and I wouldn't blame anybody for wanting to see Fahey play before putting money on him. But I don't think Ohio State needs him to throw for 350 yards to win this game. The Buckeyes have a defense allowing 13.4 points a night, and they're facing a USC offensive line that just gave up five sacks and couldn't open a running lane against Wisconsin. That's the matchup I keep coming back to. USC is dangerous when Maiava has time. He can throw it around, and Lincoln Riley knows how to create scoring chances. But if Ohio State takes away the run and starts getting pressure, I think USC spends a lot of this game trying to get out of third-and-long. Fahey might make a mistake or two. That's the risk. But I'll trust the Buckeyes' defense and take Ohio State to win by more than a touchdown. Under 53.5 was our original total pick, and I still like the idea of a lower-scoring game. The number has moved down, though, so I'd be much happier with 53.5 than the 50.5 being offered at some books now. Ohio State is going to be careful with Fahey in his first start. I don't expect Day to ask him to throw the ball 40 times unless the Buckeyes fall behind. On the other side, USC just scored seven points against Wisconsin and now faces a defense allowing only 13.4 per game. Maiava can make plays, but he needs some help up front. If the Trojans can't run the ball, those long passing downs are going to make it difficult to sustain drives. Rain could make things even tougher if it shows up Saturday night. The danger is USC giving Ohio State short fields with turnovers, or Smith breaking a couple of big plays. But I see something around 27-17 Ohio State. That gets us the Buckeyes cover and keeps the game under the original number. Final Picks: Ohio State Buckeyes -6.5 and Under 53.5 Betting on College Football? away.headline: What is the status of Ohio State's Kenyatta Jackson Jr., Jay Timmons?
away.blurb: "Last week was a great opportunity to get a bunch of guys some rest," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said. "We'll see how this week goes. ... [Most] will probably go through the rest of the week, and as we get closer to the game, we'll get an idea." Jackson was helped to the medical tent by two Ohio State athletic trainers with 11:55 remaining in the Buckeyes ' 19-15 road win on Oct. 17. He returned for the Hoosiers' final drive but then had to be helped by defensive tackle Eddrick Houston and a trainer going back to the locker room. The fifth-year defender provides crucial experience, as he's the only remaining Ohio State defensive lineman who appeared in all 16 games during the 2024 national championship run. Along with leading the Buckeyes in sacks this season (3), Jackson has played 320 snaps, according to PFF – 63 more than any other Ohio State defensive lineman. Of Jackson's 22 tackles, seven came against the Hoosiers, marking his career high. Timmons also had a career game in Bloomington, recording seven tackles, two pass breakups and a forced fumble, before being sidelined for Ohio State's final defensive drives. The freshman was dealing with an unspecified injury leading up to the Indiana game, missing the previous two matchups. In his first four Ohio State games, Timmons logged nine tackles, four pass breakups and a forced fumble in the opening drive against Texas. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State football fielded a variety of offensive line combinations through the first half of its regular season, with injuries forcing movement up front. Coming off a bye week and heading into Saturday’s game at USC, coach Ryan Day expects the unit to be as healthy as it has been this season. “We should have a full week of practice and a full arsenal of guys up front, so that is a huge deal going into this game,” Day said during a radio hit Monday on 97.1 The Fan. “We know that the offensive line, we’re going to lean on them more to be the guys who lead this team — along with our seniors, along with Jeremiah (Smith), running backs that are running real hard. But it all starts up front.” The Buckeyes opened the season with Ian Moore, Luke Montgomery, Carson Hinzman, Austin Siereveld and Phillip Daniels starting from left to right. During his absence, Ohio State originally moved Siereveld to right tackle and started Gabe VanSickle at right guard. That changed Oct. 10, when an illness sidelined Siereveld hours before a matchup with Maryland. VanSickle moved to right tackle and Jake Cook started at right guard as a result. The Buckeyes moved VanSickle back to right guard when Daniels returned to play right tackle the following week. The starting combination with a full roster remains unclear, though Day said Siereveld would start at tackle if healthy when asked ahead of the Indiana game. Health up front is always paramount, but that is especially true for a team making a change at quarterback. Julian Sayin was injured late in the win at Indiana, and the Buckeyes are preparing for him to miss the remainder of the season. As a result, freshman Luke Fahey or sophomore Tavien St. Clair will start Saturday at USC. “These guys have played a lot of football before,” Day said of the offensive line. “We’re in that huddle and you’ve got a young quarterback right there — I mean, they’re going to be looking to him, but he’s going to be looking at them. This week, however, the Trojans will be back home at the Coliseum to take on Ohio State. Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12); UCF (4-3, 2-2). Last meeting: Baylor beat UCF 30-3 on Nov. 1, 2025, in Waco What's at stake? This is an important opportunity for Baylor to get its season back on track. The Bears have dropped consecutive games against TCU and Kansas and now enter a new chapter under interim head coach Joe Klanderman following Dave Aranda's dismissal . At 4-3, Baylor cannot afford to let another conference game slip away if it hopes to remain competitive in the Big 12 standings. A road win would also give Klanderman a strong start to his tenure. UCF enters the matchup with momentum after defeating No. 2 BYU 39-31 in double overtime. The Knights have shown they can compete with the conference's top teams, making Friday's matchup an important test for Baylor's defense. When Baylor has the ball Baylor's passing attack will be one of its biggest advantages in this matchup. The Bears average 278.9 passing yards per game, and UCF surrenders 239.7 passing yards per game. Quarterback DJ Lagway will need to take advantage of that matchup and find opportunities downfield. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman has been one of Baylor's most consistent weapons, recording 58 receptions for 678 yards through seven games. His ability to create plays and stretch the field could be important against a UCF defense that has struggled more against the pass than the run. However, Baylor will need to establish a more consistent rushing attack. Dawson Pendergrass leads the Bears with 331 rushing yards, but the offense has averaged just 146.1 rushing yards per game. Finding balance between the run and pass will be important in keeping UCF's defense from focusing entirely on Lagway. When UCF has the ball The Knights rely on a balanced offensive attack led by quarterback Keyone Jenkins and running back Duke Watson. Jenkins has thrown for 1,099 yards and 11 touchdowns while Watson leads the team with 577 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Baylor's defensive front will need to pressure Jenkins and limit Watson's ability to establish the run. The Bears rank third nationally in sacks, giving them an opportunity to disrupt UCF's offensive rhythm. If Baylor can force third-and-long situations and create turnovers, it could make things difficult for a UCF offense that is coming off an emotional double-overtime victory. Baylor enters this matchup with plenty to prove after consecutive losses and a coaching change. While UCF has momentum following its win over BYU, the Bears have the defensive talent to make this a difficult matchup for the Knights. I expect Baylor to lean on its defense and take advantage of its passing game, with Freeman playing an important role. The Bears will need to clean up their mistakes and avoid giving UCF extra opportunities, but the Bears will find a way to get their first win under Klanderman. Score: Baylor 27, UCF 24. UCF is one of the more underrated teams in the country, which I've been telling you since August. And despite their injuries, they're playing solid, team football, and that culminated with a with vs. BYU. But it was not a fluke. They led Houston in the second half on the road. They were beating Oklahoma State in Stillwater early in the game. This team can play with the best. Now, they get a chance to play one of the worst? I'll not overcomplicate this and take UCF to win and cover. Baylor's run defense ranks 4th in the Big 12, but they've already played the three worst running teams in the conference in Colorado, Arizona State and TCU. Now, they get Duke Watson, Jenkins and the rest of the run game going on Friday night to seal a win. UCF wins. UCF covers. away.headline: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure
away.blurb: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure Skip to main content SI.COM Here are five of the most questionable decisions of Aranda's Baylor tenure. Aranda had reason to overhaul Baylor's defensive staff following the 2022 season, but his choice of replacement proved questionable. Continuing to direct the defense while overseeing the entire program raised questions about whether Aranda had taken on too much. Although his defensive expertise was never in doubt, the arrangement potentially limited the attention he could devote to recruiting, roster construction and other head coaching duties. Dave Aranda's tenure at Baylor peaked in 2021, when the Bears won a program-record 12 games, captured the Big 12 championship and claimed a Sugar Bowl victory. Nearly five years later, he was fired following Saturday's 25-24 loss at Kansas, finishing his six-plus seasons in Waco with a 40-40 record. Baylor's decline can't be traced to a single mistake, but several of Aranda's decisions played a role in the program's inability to sustain its success. Some made sense at the time but ultimately backfired, while others were mistakes he later acknowledged. 1. Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Baylor added only 10 scholarship transfers during Aranda's first three seasons before bringing in 12 during the 2023 cycle. While other programs increasingly used the portal to address immediate needs, the Bears remained more reliant on developing players already on their roster. Aranda later acknowledged struggling with bringing in transfers when doing so could mean passing over players he had recruited and developed. That reluctance became particularly costly following the 2021 season, when Baylor lost several important contributors, including Jalen Pitre, JT Woods, Terrel Bernard and Abram Smith. Replacing that experience and production was never going to be easy, but the transfer portal offered opportunities to address weaknesses before they became bigger problems. Instead, Baylor struggled to maintain the depth and physicality that had helped it win the conference championship.
